source.text: וַיֹּ֨סֶף֙ אַף־יְהוָ֔ה לַחֲר֖וֹת בְּיִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וַיָּ֨סֶת אֶת־דָּוִ֤ד בָּהֶם֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר לֵ֛ךְ מְנֵ֥ה אֶת־יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל וְאֶת־יְהוּדָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And again [the] anger of Yahweh burned against Israel, and he incited David against them, saying, Go, count Israel and Judah.

en.L: And again the anger of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} burned against Israel, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} incited David against them, saying, "Go, count Israel and Judah."
en.B: Once more the anger of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} flared up against Israel, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} stirred David up against them, saying, "Go and count Israel and Judah."
en.R: Once more {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} was angry with Israel. So {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} moved David to do something that would bring harm on the people. He put this idea in David's mind: "Go and count the people of Israel and Judah."

es.L: Y otra vez se encendió la ira {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} contra Israel, e {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} incitó a David contra ellos, diciendo: «Ve, cuenta a Israel y a Judá».
es.B: Una vez más la ira {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} se encendió contra Israel, e {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} incitó a David contra ellos, diciéndole: «Ve y haz un censo de Israel y de Judá».
es.R: Una vez más {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} se enojó con Israel. Así que {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} movió a David a hacer algo que traería daño al pueblo. Le puso esta idea en la mente: «Ve y cuenta a la gente de Israel y de Judá».

fr.L: Et la colère {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} s’enflamma de nouveau contre Israël, et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} incita David contre eux, disant : « Va, dénombre Israël et Juda. »
fr.B: Une fois encore, la colère {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} s’enflamma contre Israël, et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} poussa David contre eux, en lui disant : « Va faire le dénombrement d’Israël et de Juda. »
fr.R: Une fois encore, {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} s’est mis en colère contre Israël. Alors {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} a poussé David à faire une chose qui allait faire du mal au peuple. Il lui a mis cette idée en tête : « Va compter les gens d’Israël et de Juda. »

sw.L: Tena hasira ya {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} ikawaka juu ya Israeli, {{deity_pronoun:naye|Naye}} akamchochea Daudi dhidi yao, akisema, "Nenda, uwahesabu Israeli na Yuda."
sw.B: Kwa mara nyingine hasira ya {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} ikawaka dhidi ya Israeli, {{deity_pronoun:naye|Naye}} akamchochea Daudi dhidi yao, akisema, "Nenda ukawahesabu Israeli na Yuda."
sw.R: Kwa mara nyingine {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} aliwakasirikia Israeli. Kwa hiyo akamwongoza Daudi kufanya jambo ambalo lingewaletea watu madhara. Akatia wazo hili moyoni mwa Daudi: "Nenda ukawahesabu watu wa Israeli na Yuda."

vi.L: Cơn giận của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} lại nổi lên cùng Y-sơ-ra-ên, và {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} xui giục Đa-vít chống lại họ mà rằng: "Hãy đi kiểm tra dân số Y-sơ-ra-ên và Giu-đa."
vi.B: Một lần nữa cơn giận của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} bừng lên cùng Y-sơ-ra-ên, và {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} khiến Đa-vít làm điều có hại cho họ: "Hãy đi kiểm tra dân số Y-sơ-ra-ên và Giu-đa."
vi.R: Một lần nữa {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} nổi giận với Y-sơ-ra-ên. Vì vậy {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} khiến Đa-vít làm một việc sẽ đem tai họa đến cho dân chúng. Ngài đặt ý nghĩ này vào lòng Đa-vít: "Hãy đi đếm dân Y-sơ-ra-ên và Giu-đa."

ko.L: {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 진노가 다시 이스라엘을 향해 타올랐다. 그분께서 다윗을 부추겨 그들을 거스르게 하시며 말씀하셨다. "가서 이스라엘과 유다를 세어라."
ko.B: {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 진노가 다시 이스라엘을 향해 불타올랐다. 그분께서 다윗을 부추겨 그들에게 해가 되게 하시며 말씀하셨다. "가서 이스라엘과 유다의 인구를 세어라."
ko.R: {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 또다시 이스라엘에게 노하셨다. 그래서 그분께서는 다윗이 백성에게 해가 될 일을 하게 하셨다. 그분께서 다윗의 마음에 이런 생각을 넣으셨다. "가서 이스라엘과 유다의 백성을 세어 보아라."

pt.L: E de novo a ira {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}} se acendeu contra Israel, e {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} incitou Davi contra eles, dizendo: "Vai, conta Israel e Judá."
pt.B: Mais uma vez a ira {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}} se inflamou contra Israel, e {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} instigou Davi contra eles, dizendo: "Vai e conta Israel e Judá."
pt.R: Mais uma vez {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} ficou irado com Israel. Por isso {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} levou Davi a fazer algo que traria mal ao povo. Ele pôs esta ideia na mente de Davi: "Vai e conta o povo de Israel e de Judá."

decisions.choice: he incited David: Yahweh is the one who moves David to act
decisions.reason: The sentence runs straight on from "the anger of Yahweh", so the one who incites David is Yahweh. 1 Chronicles 21:1, telling the same story, says instead that Satan (or "an adversary") rose up against Israel and incited David. The two accounts look at one event from two sides. Elsewhere too Scripture speaks of God carrying out judgment through a hostile agent (1 Samuel 16:14; 1 Kings 22:19-23), and in Job 2:3 the same verb is used of the adversary inciting God against Job. Neither account excuses David: he confesses the census as his own sin (verse 10).

decisions.choice: again: a second outbreak of Yahweh's anger, after the famine of 21:1-14
decisions.reason: The famine in 21:1-14 ended when "God was entreated for the land" (21:14). This story ends with the same words (verse 25). The text does not say what Israel had done to provoke this second anger.

decisions.choice: count Israel and Judah: a census of the men able to fight
decisions.reason: The count is of fighting men (verse 9), carried out by the army commanders (verse 4). Counting the people was not wrong in itself (Numbers 1:2-3; 26:2), but the law warned that a census without a ransom for each life would bring a plague (Exodus 30:12). The text does not say exactly where David's fault lay; Joab's protest (verse 3) and David's confession (verse 10) show that there was one.

decisions.choice: against them: to their harm
decisions.reason: David is moved to do something that will turn out against Israel. The people suffer the result in the plague (verse 15).

decisions.choice: moved David to do something that would bring harm on the people; put this idea in David's mind
decisions.reason: Readable explains "incited against them" and shows that "saying" here gives the thought that was put into David's mind, not words he heard aloud.

decisions.choice: incitó a David contra ellos
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says plainly that the LORD incited David; Spanish keeps the subject as the Hebrew and the English do, and the meaning decisions explain how 1 Chronicles 21:1 tells it.

decisions.choice: "kiểm tra dân số" (L, B); "đếm dân" (R)
decisions.reason: The census counts the men able to fight (meaning decision); "kiểm tra dân số" is the plain Vietnamese for counting a people, and Readable says simply "count".

decisions.choice: contar (this verse, verse 10); recensear (L, B) and contar (R) for "register" (verses 2, 4); o recenseamento (verse 9)
decisions.reason: For the whole chapter, the words of the census in Numbers 1:2-3 in Portuguese: the plain verb "count" is "contar" at every level, and the verb of the military muster (verses 2, 4, 9) is "recensear" at Literal and Balanced and "contar" at Readable. The command comes from the LORD to one man, so it takes "tu" ("Vai, conta").

source.text: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר הַמֶּ֜לֶךְ אֶל־יוֹאָ֣ב׀שַׂר־הַחַ֣יִל אֲשֶׁר־אִתּ֗וֹ שֽׁוּט־נָ֞א בְּכָל־שִׁבְטֵ֤י יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ מִדָּן֙ וְעַד־בְּאֵ֣ר שֶׁ֔בַע וּפִקְד֖וּ אֶת־הָעָ֑ם וְיָ֣דַעְתִּ֔י אֵ֖ת מִסְפַּ֥ר הָעָֽם׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And said the king to Joab, commander of the army who [was] with him, Go about, please, through all [the] tribes of Israel from Dan and to Beer-sheba, and enroll the people, and I will know the number of the people.

en.L: And the king said to Joab, the commander of the army who [was] with him, "Go about, please, through all the tribes of Israel, from Dan to Beersheba, and register the people, so that I may know the number of the people."
en.B: So the king said to Joab, the commander of the army who was with him, "Go through all the tribes of Israel, from Dan to Beersheba, and register the people, so that I may know how many there are."
en.R: So King David said to Joab, the army commander who was with him, "Go through all the tribes of Israel, from Dan in the far north to Beersheba in the far south. Count the people, so that I will know how many there are."

es.L: Y el rey dijo a Joab, jefe del ejército, que [estaba] con él: «Recorre, te ruego, todas las tribus de Israel, desde Dan hasta Beerseba, y haz el censo del pueblo, para que yo sepa el número del pueblo».
es.B: Así que el rey le dijo a Joab, el jefe del ejército que estaba con él: «Recorre todas las tribus de Israel, desde Dan hasta Beerseba, y haz el censo del pueblo, para que yo sepa cuántos son».
es.R: Entonces el rey David le dijo a Joab, el jefe del ejército que estaba con él: «Recorre todas las tribus de Israel, desde Dan en el extremo norte hasta Beerseba en el extremo sur. Cuenta a la gente, para que yo sepa cuántos son».

fr.L: Et le roi dit à Joab, le chef de l’armée, qui [était] avec lui : « Parcours donc toutes les tribus d’Israël, depuis Dan jusqu’à Beer-Shéba, et recensez le peuple, afin que je connaisse le nombre du peuple. »
fr.B: Le roi dit donc à Joab, le chef de l’armée, qui était avec lui : « Parcours toutes les tribus d’Israël, depuis Dan jusqu’à Beer-Shéba, et recensez le peuple, afin que je sache combien ils sont. »
fr.R: Le roi David a donc dit à Joab, le chef de l’armée, qui était avec lui : « Parcours toutes les tribus d’Israël, depuis Dan, tout au nord, jusqu’à Beer-Shéba, tout au sud. Comptez les gens, pour que je sache combien ils sont. »

sw.L: Mfalme akamwambia Yoabu, jemadari wa jeshi aliyekuwa pamoja naye, "Tafadhali zunguka katika makabila yote ya Israeli, tangu Dani mpaka Beer-sheba, uwaandikishe watu, ili nijue idadi ya watu."
sw.B: Basi mfalme akamwambia Yoabu, mkuu wa jeshi aliyekuwa pamoja naye, "Pita katika makabila yote ya Israeli, tangu Dani mpaka Beer-sheba, uwaandikishe watu, ili nijue wako wangapi."
sw.R: Basi Mfalme Daudi akamwambia Yoabu, mkuu wa jeshi aliyekuwa pamoja naye, "Pita katika makabila yote ya Israeli, tangu Dani kule kaskazini kabisa mpaka Beer-sheba kule kusini kabisa. Wahesabu watu, ili nijue wako wangapi."

vi.L: Vua nói với Giô-áp, tướng chỉ huy quân đội đang ở với vua: "Hãy đi khắp các chi tộc Y-sơ-ra-ên, từ Đan đến Bê-e-Sê-ba, và ghi danh dân chúng, để ta biết số dân."
vi.B: Vậy vua nói với Giô-áp, tướng chỉ huy quân đội đang ở với mình: "Hãy đi khắp các chi tộc Y-sơ-ra-ên, từ Đan đến Bê-e-Sê-ba, mà ghi danh dân chúng, để ta biết họ có bao nhiêu người."
vi.R: Vậy vua Đa-vít nói với Giô-áp, tướng chỉ huy quân đội đang ở với vua: "Hãy đi khắp các chi tộc Y-sơ-ra-ên, từ Đan ở tận miền bắc đến Bê-e-Sê-ba ở tận miền nam. Hãy đếm dân, để ta biết họ có bao nhiêu người."

ko.L: 왕이 자기와 함께 있는 군대 사령관 요압에게 말했다. "부디 단에서 브엘세바까지 이스라엘의 모든 지파를 두루 다니며 백성을 등록하여라. 그러면 내가 백성의 수를 알겠다."
ko.B: 그래서 왕은 자기와 함께 있던 군대 사령관 요압에게 말했다. "단에서 브엘세바까지 이스라엘의 모든 지파를 두루 다니며 백성을 등록하여라. 백성이 얼마나 되는지 알아야겠다."
ko.R: 그래서 다윗 왕은 자기와 함께 있던 군대 사령관 요압에게 말했다. "북쪽 끝 단에서 남쪽 끝 브엘세바까지 이스라엘의 모든 지파를 다니며 백성을 세어라. 그러면 백성이 얼마나 되는지 알 수 있을 것이다."

pt.L: E o rei disse a Joabe, o comandante do exército, que [estava] com ele: "Percorra, por favor, todas as tribos de Israel, desde Dã até Berseba, e recenseiem o povo, para que eu saiba o número do povo."
pt.B: Então o rei disse a Joabe, o comandante do exército, que estava com ele: "Percorra todas as tribos de Israel, de Dã até Berseba, e recenseiem o povo, para que eu saiba quantos são."
pt.R: Então o rei Davi disse a Joabe, o comandante do exército, que estava com ele: "Vá por todas as tribos de Israel, desde Dã, no extremo norte, até Berseba, no extremo sul. Contem o povo, para que eu saiba quantos são."

decisions.choice: register: enroll men for military service
decisions.reason: The verb means to muster or enroll, the word used for the census of fighting men in Numbers 1:3 and 26:2. It is more than a head count: it lists the men who can be called up.

decisions.choice: from Dan to Beersheba: the whole land, from north to south
decisions.reason: Dan was the northernmost town of Israel and Beersheba the southernmost; the pair names the whole country (1 Samuel 3:20; 3:10 and 17:11 in this book).

decisions.choice: so that I may know the number: the purpose of the count
decisions.reason: David states his reason: he wants to know how many men he has. Joab's reply (verse 3) questions whether that is a good reason.

decisions.choice: King David; in the far north ... in the far south
decisions.reason: Readable names the king and says where Dan and Beersheba lay, as it does at 3:10.

decisions.choice: Percorra (você) ... recenseiem (vocês)
decisions.reason: The king speaks to Joab, his subject, with "você", and the second verb turns to the plural, "recenseiem", as the Hebrew does, since Joab and his commanders carry out the count (verse 4).

source.text: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר יוֹאָ֜ב אֶל־הַמֶּ֗לֶךְ וְיוֹסֵ֣ף יְהוָה֩ אֱלֹהֶ֨יךָ אֶל־הָעָ֜ם כָּהֵ֤ם׀וְכָהֵם֙ מֵאָ֣ה פְעָמִ֔ים וְעֵינֵ֥י אֲדֹנִֽי־הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ רֹא֑וֹת וַאדֹנִ֣י הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ לָ֥מָּה חָפֵ֖ץ בַּדָּבָ֥ר הַזֶּֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And said Joab to the king, And may add Yahweh your God to the people as they [are] and as they [are] a hundred times, and [the] eyes of my lord the king [be] seeing; but my lord the king, why does he delight in this thing?

en.L: And Joab said to the king, "May {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God add to the people as they [are] and as they [are], a hundred times, while the eyes of my lord the king see [it]! But why does my lord the king delight in this thing?"
en.B: But Joab said to the king, "May {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God make the people a hundred times as many as they are, and may my lord the king see it with his own eyes! But why does my lord the king want to do this?"
en.R: But Joab answered the king, "I pray that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God will make your people a hundred times more than they are now, and that you will live to see it, my king. But why do you want to do this?"

es.L: Y Joab dijo al rey: «¡Que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} tu Dios añada al pueblo tanto como son y tanto como son, cien veces, y que los ojos de mi señor el rey [lo] vean! Pero ¿por qué se complace mi señor el rey en esta cosa?».
es.B: Pero Joab le dijo al rey: «¡Que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} tu Dios haga al pueblo cien veces más numeroso de lo que es, y que mi señor el rey lo vea con sus propios ojos! Pero ¿por qué quiere mi señor el rey hacer esto?».
es.R: Pero Joab le respondió al rey: «Le pido a {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} tu Dios que haga a tu pueblo cien veces más numeroso de lo que es ahora, y que tú vivas para verlo, mi rey. Pero ¿por qué quieres hacer esto?».

fr.L: Et Joab dit au roi : « Que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} ton Dieu ajoute au peuple autant et autant qu’ils sont, cent fois, et que les yeux de mon seigneur le roi le voient ! Mais pourquoi mon seigneur le roi prend-il plaisir à cette chose ? »
fr.B: Mais Joab dit au roi : « Que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} ton Dieu rende le peuple cent fois plus nombreux qu’il ne l’est, et que mon seigneur le roi le voie de ses propres yeux ! Mais pourquoi mon seigneur le roi veut-il faire cela ? »
fr.R: Mais Joab a répondu au roi : « Je prie pour que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} ton Dieu rende ton peuple cent fois plus nombreux qu’il ne l’est maintenant, et que tu vives assez longtemps pour le voir, mon roi. Mais pourquoi veux-tu faire cela ? »

sw.L: Yoabu akamwambia mfalme, "{{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wako na awaongeze watu kama walivyo na kama walivyo, mara mia, macho ya bwana wangu mfalme yakiona! Lakini kwa nini bwana wangu mfalme anapendezwa na jambo hili?"
sw.B: Lakini Yoabu akamwambia mfalme, "{{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wako na awazidishe watu mara mia kuliko walivyo sasa, na bwana wangu mfalme ajionee kwa macho yake mwenyewe! Lakini kwa nini bwana wangu mfalme anataka kufanya jambo hili?"
sw.R: Lakini Yoabu akamjibu mfalme, "Naomba {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wako awafanye watu wako kuwa wengi mara mia kuliko walivyo sasa, nawe uishi kuliona hilo, mfalme wangu. Lakini kwa nini unataka kufanya jambo hili?"

vi.L: Giô-áp nói với vua: "Nguyện {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Đức Chúa Trời của vua thêm số dân lên, dù họ [nhiều] bao nhiêu, gấp trăm lần, trong khi mắt chúa tôi là vua còn thấy [điều đó]! Nhưng sao chúa tôi là vua lại thích việc này?"
vi.B: Nhưng Giô-áp thưa với vua: "Nguyện {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Đức Chúa Trời của bệ hạ làm cho dân chúng đông gấp trăm lần hiện nay, và nguyện bệ hạ được tận mắt nhìn thấy! Nhưng sao bệ hạ lại muốn làm việc này?"
vi.R: Nhưng Giô-áp thưa với vua: "Tôi cầu xin {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Đức Chúa Trời của đức vua làm cho dân của đức vua đông gấp trăm lần hiện nay, và đức vua được sống để thấy điều đó. Nhưng sao đức vua lại muốn làm việc này?"

ko.L: 요압이 왕에게 말했다. "임금님의 하나님 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 백성을 지금보다 백 배나 더하시고, 내 주 임금님의 눈이 [그것을] 보시기를 바랍니다. 그런데 내 주 임금님께서는 어찌하여 이 일을 원하십니까?"
ko.B: 그러나 요압이 왕에게 말했다. "임금님의 하나님 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 백성을 지금보다 백 배나 많게 하시고, 내 주 임금님께서 그것을 친히 보시기를 바랍니다. 그런데 내 주 임금님께서는 왜 이 일을 하려고 하십니까?"
ko.R: 그러나 요압이 왕에게 대답했다. "임금님의 하나님 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 임금님의 백성을 지금보다 백 배나 많게 하시고, 임금님께서 살아 계셔서 그것을 보시기를 빕니다. 그런데 임금님, 왜 이 일을 하려고 하십니까?"

pt.L: E Joabe disse ao rei: "Que {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}}, o seu Deus, acrescente ao povo tantos quantos eles [são], cem vezes, enquanto os olhos do meu senhor, o rei, [o] veem! Mas por que o meu senhor, o rei, se agrada desta coisa?"
pt.B: Mas Joabe disse ao rei: "Que {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}}, o seu Deus, multiplique o povo cem vezes mais do que ele é, e que o meu senhor, o rei, o veja com os próprios olhos! Mas por que o meu senhor, o rei, quer fazer isso?"
pt.R: Mas Joabe respondeu ao rei: "Peço que {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}}, o seu Deus, faça o seu povo cem vezes maior do que é agora, e que o senhor viva para ver isso, meu rei. Mas por que o senhor quer fazer isso?"

decisions.choice: as they are and as they are: as many as they now are
decisions.reason: The doubled phrase means "however many they are". Joab wishes that the people may grow to a hundred times their present size.

decisions.choice: while the eyes of my lord the king see it: may the king live to see it
decisions.reason: The clause describes the time of the increase: may it happen in David's own lifetime.

decisions.choice: delight in: want, desire
decisions.reason: The verb means to take pleasure in or to want something. Joab's point is that growth comes from Yahweh, so there is no need for the king to count what Yahweh gives. He objects, but does not say what is wrong with the census.

decisions.choice: my king; you
decisions.reason: Joab speaks of the king in the third person, as a courtier did. Readable lets him speak to David directly.

decisions.choice: o meu senhor, o rei (L, B); o senhor, meu rei (R)
decisions.reason: Joab speaks of the king in the courtly third person (m1), as subjects do to David throughout the book in Portuguese; "o seu Deus" goes with it. Readable lets him speak to David directly with "o senhor", as the English Readable says "you".

source.text: וַיֶּחֱזַ֤ק דְּבַר־הַמֶּ֨לֶךְ֙ אֶל־יוֹאָ֔ב וְעַ֖ל שָׂרֵ֣י הֶחָ֑יִל וַיֵּצֵ֨א יוֹאָ֜ב וְשָׂרֵ֤י הַחַ֨יִל֙ לִפְנֵ֣י הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ לִפְקֹ֥ד אֶת־הָעָ֖ם אֶת־יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

records.literal_gloss: And prevailed [the] word of the king against Joab and against [the] commanders of the army, and went out Joab and [the] commanders of the army from before the king to enroll the people, Israel.

en.L: But the king's word prevailed against Joab and against the commanders of the army. So Joab and the commanders of the army went out from before the king to register the people, Israel.
en.B: But the king's order overruled Joab and the army commanders, so Joab and the commanders of the army left the king's presence to register the people of Israel.
en.R: But the king would not change his order, even though Joab and the army commanders were against it. So they left the king and went out to count the people of Israel.

es.L: Pero la palabra del rey prevaleció sobre Joab y sobre los jefes del ejército. Y salieron Joab y los jefes del ejército de delante del rey para hacer el censo del pueblo, de Israel.
es.B: Pero la orden del rey se impuso a Joab y a los jefes del ejército, así que Joab y los jefes del ejército salieron de la presencia del rey para hacer el censo del pueblo de Israel.
es.R: Pero el rey no quiso cambiar su orden, aunque Joab y los jefes del ejército estaban en contra. Así que dejaron al rey y salieron a contar a la gente de Israel.

fr.L: Mais la parole du roi l’emporta sur Joab et sur les chefs de l’armée. Et Joab et les chefs de l’armée sortirent de devant le roi pour recenser le peuple, Israël.
fr.B: Mais l’ordre du roi s’imposa à Joab et aux chefs de l’armée, et Joab et les chefs de l’armée quittèrent le roi pour recenser le peuple d’Israël.
fr.R: Mais le roi n’a pas voulu changer son ordre, même si Joab et les chefs de l’armée n’étaient pas d’accord. Ils ont donc quitté le roi et ils sont partis compter le peuple d’Israël.

sw.L: Lakini neno la mfalme likamshinda Yoabu na majemadari wa jeshi. Basi Yoabu na majemadari wa jeshi wakatoka mbele ya mfalme ili kuwaandikisha watu, Israeli.
sw.B: Lakini amri ya mfalme ikashinda maoni ya Yoabu na makamanda wa jeshi, kwa hiyo Yoabu na makamanda wa jeshi wakaondoka mbele ya mfalme kwenda kuwaandikisha watu wa Israeli.
sw.R: Lakini mfalme hakubadili amri yake, ingawa Yoabu na makamanda wa jeshi waliipinga. Kwa hiyo wakamwacha mfalme, wakaenda kuwahesabu watu wa Israeli.

vi.L: Nhưng lời vua thắng Giô-áp và các tướng chỉ huy quân đội. Vậy Giô-áp và các tướng chỉ huy quân đội ra khỏi trước mặt vua để ghi danh dân chúng, là Y-sơ-ra-ên.
vi.B: Nhưng lệnh của vua đã gạt bỏ ý kiến của Giô-áp và các tướng chỉ huy quân đội, nên Giô-áp và các tướng rời khỏi trước mặt vua để ghi danh dân Y-sơ-ra-ên.
vi.R: Nhưng vua không chịu đổi lệnh, dù Giô-áp và các tướng chỉ huy quân đội phản đối. Vậy họ rời khỏi vua và đi đếm dân Y-sơ-ra-ên.

ko.L: 그러나 왕의 말이 요압과 군대 지휘관들을 이겼다. 그래서 요압과 군대 지휘관들이 이스라엘 백성을 등록하려고 왕 앞에서 나갔다.
ko.B: 그러나 요압과 군대 지휘관들은 왕의 명령을 꺾지 못했다. 그래서 요압과 군대 지휘관들은 이스라엘 백성을 등록하려고 왕 앞에서 물러 나왔다.
ko.R: 그러나 요압과 군대 지휘관들이 반대했는데도 왕은 명령을 바꾸지 않았다. 그래서 그들은 왕 앞에서 물러 나와 이스라엘 백성을 세러 나갔다.

pt.L: Mas a palavra do rei prevaleceu sobre Joabe e sobre os comandantes do exército. E Joabe e os comandantes do exército saíram de diante do rei para recensear o povo, Israel.
pt.B: Mas a ordem do rei se impôs a Joabe e aos comandantes do exército. Então Joabe e os comandantes do exército saíram da presença do rei para recensear o povo de Israel.
pt.R: Mas o rei não quis mudar a sua ordem, mesmo com Joabe e os comandantes do exército contra ela. Então eles deixaram o rei e saíram para contar o povo de Israel.

decisions.choice: the king's word prevailed against: the king overruled them
decisions.reason: The verb means "was strong against". The king's command won over the objection of Joab and, it seems, of the other commanders too, since they are named alongside him.

decisions.choice: commanders of the army: the senior military officers
decisions.reason: The census of fighting men was carried out by the army's own officers, as a military muster.

decisions.choice: the people, Israel: the two words name the same group
decisions.reason: "Israel" explains "the people": the whole nation is to be counted.

decisions.choice: would not change his order, even though Joab and the army commanders were against it
decisions.reason: Readable spells out what "prevailed against" implies: the commanders objected and were overruled.

source.text: וַיַּעַבְר֖וּ אֶת־הַיַּרְדֵּ֑ן וַיַּחֲנ֣וּ בַעֲרוֹעֵ֗ר יְמִ֥ין הָעִ֛יר אֲשֶׁ֛ר בְּתוֹךְ־הַנַּ֥חַל הַגָּ֖ד וְאֶל־יַעְזֵֽר׃

records.literal_gloss: And they crossed the Jordan and camped in Aroer, south of the city which [is] in [the] middle of the valley, the Gad, and to Jazer.

en.L: And they crossed the Jordan and camped at Aroer, south of the city that [is] in the middle of the valley, toward Gad and to Jazer.
en.B: They crossed the Jordan and camped at Aroer, on the south side of the town in the middle of the valley; then they went through Gad and on to Jazer.
en.R: They crossed the Jordan River and set up camp at Aroer, south of the town that stands in the middle of the valley. Then they went through the land of the tribe of Gad and on to Jazer.

es.L: Y pasaron el Jordán y acamparon en Aroer, al sur de la ciudad que [está] en medio del valle, hacia Gad y hasta Jazer.
es.B: Cruzaron el Jordán y acamparon en Aroer, al sur de la ciudad que está en medio del valle; luego fueron por Gad y siguieron hasta Jazer.
es.R: Cruzaron el río Jordán y acamparon en Aroer, al sur de la ciudad que está en medio del valle. Luego pasaron por la tierra de la tribu de Gad y siguieron hasta Jazer.

fr.L: Et ils passèrent le Jourdain et campèrent à Aroër, au sud de la ville qui [est] au milieu de la vallée, vers Gad et jusqu’à Yazer.
fr.B: Ils passèrent le Jourdain et campèrent à Aroër, au sud de la ville qui est au milieu de la vallée ; puis ils traversèrent Gad et allèrent jusqu’à Yazer.
fr.R: Ils ont traversé le Jourdain et ils ont installé leur camp à Aroër, au sud de la ville qui se trouve au milieu de la vallée. Ensuite, ils ont traversé le territoire de la tribu de Gad et sont allés jusqu’à Yazer.

sw.L: Wakavuka Yordani wakapiga kambi Aroeri, upande wa kusini wa mji ulio katikati ya bonde, kuelekea Gadi na mpaka Yazeri.
sw.B: Wakavuka Yordani wakapiga kambi Aroeri, upande wa kusini wa mji ulio katikati ya bonde; kisha wakapita Gadi mpaka Yazeri.
sw.R: Wakavuka mto Yordani, wakapiga kambi Aroeri, upande wa kusini wa mji uliosimama katikati ya bonde. Kisha wakapita katika nchi ya kabila la Gadi mpaka Yazeri.

vi.L: Họ qua sông Giô-đanh và đóng trại tại A-rô-e, phía nam thành ở giữa thung lũng, về hướng Gát, và đến Gia-ê-xe.
vi.B: Họ qua sông Giô-đanh và đóng trại tại A-rô-e, phía nam thành nằm giữa thung lũng; rồi họ đi qua đất Gát và đến Gia-ê-xe.
vi.R: Họ qua sông Giô-đanh và đóng trại tại A-rô-e, phía nam thành nằm giữa thung lũng. Rồi họ đi qua đất của chi tộc Gát và đến Gia-ê-xe.

ko.L: 그들은 요단강을 건너, 골짜기 한가운데 있는 성읍의 남쪽 아로엘에 진을 치고, 갓 쪽으로 [가서] 야셀에 이르렀다.
ko.B: 그들은 요단강을 건너, 골짜기 한가운데 있는 성읍의 남쪽 아로엘에 진을 쳤다. 그다음에 갓을 거쳐 야셀까지 갔다.
ko.R: 그들은 요단강을 건너 아로엘에 진을 쳤는데, 그곳은 골짜기 한가운데 있는 성읍의 남쪽이었다. 그다음에 갓 지파의 땅을 지나 야셀까지 갔다.

pt.L: E atravessaram o Jordão e acamparam em Aroer, ao sul da cidade que [está] no meio do vale, em direção a Gade e até Jazer.
pt.B: Eles atravessaram o Jordão e acamparam em Aroer, ao sul da cidade que fica no meio do vale; depois passaram por Gade e seguiram até Jazer.
pt.R: Eles atravessaram o rio Jordão e acamparam em Aroer, ao sul da cidade que fica no meio do vale. Depois passaram pela terra da tribo de Gade e foram até Jazer.

decisions.choice: Aroer: the southern edge of Israel's land east of the Jordan
decisions.reason: Aroer stood on the edge of the Arnon gorge, with "the city in the middle of the valley" near it (Deuteronomy 2:36; Joshua 13:9, 16). The counters start in the far southeast and go north through the land east of the Jordan, then west and south (verses 6-7), around the whole country.

decisions.choice: camped: the Hebrew text as it stands
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says they camped at Aroer. The ancient Greek translation reads "they began at Aroer", a few letters different in Hebrew, which fits the account of a route. The Hebrew reading makes sense as the first stop of the journey and is kept; reviewers should check the evidence.

decisions.choice: the Gad, and to Jazer: on through the territory of Gad to Jazer
decisions.reason: "The Gad" has no preposition and may name the valley ("the valley of Gad") or the territory of the tribe of Gad (Numbers 32:34-36). Either way the route runs north through Gad to Jazer, a town in Gad's land (Joshua 13:25).

decisions.choice: and then went through Gad (Balanced); went through the land of the tribe of Gad (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable supply the movement the Hebrew implies; Readable also adds "River" and "the land of the tribe".

decisions.choice: Aroër, Yazer
decisions.reason: French transcriptions, with the diaeresis for the separate vowel and "y" for the Hebrew yod; kept for both books.

decisions.choice: Aroeri, Gadi, Yazeri
decisions.reason: Places in the census route of verses 5-7 that are not in the terms note follow the usual Swahili pattern; Gad is "Gadi", as the tribe in the Swahili Pentateuch, and Tyre is "Tiro", as the terms note.

decisions.choice: "A-rô-e", "Gát" (the tribe's land), "Gia-ê-xe"
decisions.reason: Usual Vietnamese forms; Gad takes the form of the Vietnamese Genesis.

source.text: וַיָּבֹ֨אוּ֙ הַגִּלְעָ֔דָה וְאֶל־אֶ֥רֶץ תַּחְתִּ֖ים חָדְשִׁ֑י וַיָּבֹ֨אוּ֙ דָּ֣נָה יַּ֔עַן וְסָבִ֖יב אֶל־צִידֽוֹן׃

records.literal_gloss: And they came to Gilead and to [the] land of Tahtim-hodshi, and they came to Dan-jaan and around to Sidon.

en.L: And they came to Gilead and to the land of Tahtim-hodshi, and they came to Dan-jaan and around to Sidon.
en.B: Then they went to Gilead and the land of Tahtim-hodshi, came on to Dan-jaan, and went around toward Sidon.
en.R: Next they went north to the region of Gilead and to the land of Tahtim-hodshi. They came to Dan-jaan and went around toward the city of Sidon.

es.L: Y llegaron a Galaad y a la tierra de Tahtim-hodsi, y llegaron a Dan-jaán y alrededor hacia Sidón.
es.B: Luego fueron a Galaad y a la tierra de Tahtim-hodsi, siguieron hasta Dan-jaán y dieron la vuelta hacia Sidón.
es.R: Después fueron al norte, a la región de Galaad y a la tierra de Tahtim-hodsi. Llegaron a Dan-jaán y dieron la vuelta hacia la ciudad de Sidón.

fr.L: Et ils allèrent en Galaad et au pays de Tahtim-Hodshi, et ils allèrent à Dan-Yaân et aux environs de Sidon.
fr.B: Puis ils allèrent en Galaad et au pays de Tahtim-Hodshi, ils arrivèrent à Dan-Yaân et firent le tour vers Sidon.
fr.R: Ensuite, ils sont montés vers le nord, dans la région de Galaad et au pays de Tahtim-Hodshi. Ils sont arrivés à Dan-Yaân, puis ils ont fait le tour vers la ville de Sidon.

sw.L: Wakafika Gileadi na nchi ya Tahtim-hodshi, wakafika Dani-yaani na kuzunguka mpaka Sidoni.
sw.B: Kisha wakaenda Gileadi na nchi ya Tahtim-hodshi, wakaendelea mpaka Dani-yaani, wakazunguka kuelekea Sidoni.
sw.R: Kisha wakaenda kaskazini mpaka eneo la Gileadi na nchi ya Tahtim-hodshi. Wakafika Dani-yaani na kuzunguka kuelekea mji wa Sidoni.

vi.L: Họ đến Ga-la-át và đến đất Ta-tim Hốt-si, rồi đến Đan-Gia-an và vòng quanh đến Si-đôn.
vi.B: Rồi họ đến Ga-la-át và đất Ta-tim Hốt-si, đến Đan-Gia-an, rồi đi vòng về phía Si-đôn.
vi.R: Kế đến họ đi lên phía bắc, đến vùng Ga-la-át và đất Ta-tim Hốt-si. Họ đến Đan-Gia-an rồi đi vòng về phía thành Si-đôn.

ko.L: 그들은 길르앗과 닷딤홋시 땅에 이르렀고, 다냐안에 이르러 시돈으로 돌아갔다.
ko.B: 그다음에 그들은 길르앗과 닷딤홋시 땅으로 갔고, 다냐안에 이르러 시돈 쪽으로 돌아갔다.
ko.R: 그다음에 그들은 북쪽으로 올라가 길르앗 지방과 닷딤홋시 땅으로 갔다. 그리고 다냐안에 이르렀다가 시돈 성 쪽으로 돌아갔다.

pt.L: E foram a Gileade e à terra de Taitim-Hodsi, e foram a Dã-Jaã e ao redor até Sidom.
pt.B: Depois foram a Gileade e à terra de Taitim-Hodsi, chegaram a Dã-Jaã e deram a volta em direção a Sidom.
pt.R: Em seguida foram para o norte, até a região de Gileade e a terra de Taitim-Hodsi. Chegaram a Dã-Jaã e deram a volta em direção à cidade de Sidom.

decisions.choice: Tahtim-hodshi: a place name not known elsewhere
alternatives: the land of the Hittites, to Kadesh
decisions.reason: No place of this name appears anywhere else, and the words look damaged. Some manuscripts of the ancient Greek translation read "the land of the Hittites, to Kadesh", which would point to the far north, beyond Dan. The Hebrew is kept, but the name is uncertain; reviewers should check the evidence.

decisions.choice: Dan-jaan: probably Dan in the far north, or a place near it
decisions.reason: The town of Dan was the northern limit of the land (verse 2). The added word is not explained; it may name a place near Dan or be a copying error.

decisions.choice: around to Sidon: turning west toward the Phoenician coast
decisions.reason: Sidon itself was a Phoenician city outside Israel. The counters went round toward it, along the northern border of the tribe of Asher (Joshua 19:28).

decisions.choice: Tahtim-hodshi; Dan-jaan
decisions.reason: Each name is given as one hyphenated name, as two Hebrew words that together name one place.

decisions.choice: went north to the region of; the city of Sidon
decisions.reason: Readable adds the direction and calls Gilead a region and Sidon a city.

decisions.choice: Tahtim-hodsi; Dan-jaán; Aroer, Jazer, Sidón, Tiro
decisions.reason: As the English decision, the uncertain place names are kept as the Hebrew gives them, in the usual Spanish spelling; Sidón and Tiro are the forms already in the Spanish Bible.

decisions.choice: Taitim-Hodsi; Dã-Jaã
decisions.reason: The places of the route take the forms of the Pentateuch and Joshua in Portuguese (Aroer, Gade, Jazer, Gileade, Sidom, Tiro, os heveus, os cananeus, o Neguebe, Berseba, Dã). The two uncertain names (m1, m2) are written as one hyphenated name each, as the English does, with "Dã" as the town in the far north and the Portuguese spelling of the rest; their form is a draft for a reviewer to check.

source.text: וַיָּבֹ֨אוּ֙מִבְצַר־צֹ֔ר וְכָל־עָרֵ֥י הַחִוִּ֖י וְהַֽכְּנַעֲנִ֑י וַיֵּֽצְא֛וּ אֶל־נֶ֥גֶב יְהוּדָ֖ה בְּאֵ֥ר שָֽׁבַע׃

records.literal_gloss: And they came [to the] fortress of Tyre and all [the] cities of the Hivite and the Canaanite, and they went out to [the] Negev of Judah, Beer-sheba.

en.L: And they came to the fortress of Tyre and all the cities of the Hivites and the Canaanites, and they went out to the Negev of Judah, to Beersheba.
en.B: They came to the fortress of Tyre and to all the towns of the Hivites and Canaanites, and then went out to the Negev of Judah, at Beersheba.
en.R: They went to the walled city of Tyre and to all the towns where Hivites and Canaanites lived. Then they went south to the Negev, the dry southern land of Judah, and came to Beersheba.

es.L: Y llegaron a la fortaleza de Tiro y a todas las ciudades de los heveos y de los cananeos, y salieron al Néguev de Judá, a Beerseba.
es.B: Llegaron a la fortaleza de Tiro y a todas las ciudades de los heveos y de los cananeos, y luego salieron hacia el Néguev de Judá, a Beerseba.
es.R: Fueron a la ciudad amurallada de Tiro y a todos los pueblos donde vivían los heveos y los cananeos. Luego fueron al sur, al Néguev, la tierra seca del sur de Judá, y llegaron a Beerseba.

fr.L: Et ils allèrent à la forteresse de Tyr, et à toutes les villes des Hévéens et des Cananéens, et ils sortirent vers le Néguev de Juda, à Beer-Shéba.
fr.B: Ils allèrent jusqu’à la forteresse de Tyr et dans toutes les villes des Hévéens et des Cananéens, puis ils descendirent vers le Néguev de Juda, à Beer-Shéba.
fr.R: Ils sont allés jusqu’à la ville fortifiée de Tyr et dans toutes les villes où vivaient des Hévéens et des Cananéens. Puis ils sont descendus vers le sud, dans le Néguev, la région sèche au sud de Juda, et ils sont arrivés à Beer-Shéba.

sw.L: Wakafika kwenye ngome ya Tiro na miji yote ya Wahivi na Wakanaani, wakatoka kwenda Negebu ya Yuda, mpaka Beer-sheba.
sw.B: Wakafika kwenye ngome ya Tiro na miji yote ya Wahivi na Wakanaani, kisha wakatoka kwenda Negebu ya Yuda, huko Beer-sheba.
sw.R: Wakaenda kwenye mji wenye kuta wa Tiro na miji yote walimoishi Wahivi na Wakanaani. Kisha wakaenda kusini mpaka Negebu, nchi kavu ya kusini ya Yuda, wakafika Beer-sheba.

vi.L: Họ đến đồn lũy Ty-rơ và tất cả các thành của người Hê-vít và người Ca-na-an, rồi đi ra đến Nê-ghép của Giu-đa, đến Bê-e-Sê-ba.
vi.B: Họ đến đồn lũy Ty-rơ và tất cả các thành của người Hê-vít và người Ca-na-an, rồi đi ra đến Nê-ghép của Giu-đa, tại Bê-e-Sê-ba.
vi.R: Họ đến thành Ty-rơ có tường bao bọc và tất cả các thành có người Hê-vít và người Ca-na-an sinh sống. Rồi họ đi xuống phía nam đến Nê-ghép, là vùng đất khô cằn phía nam Giu-đa, và đến Bê-e-Sê-ba.

ko.L: 그들은 두로 요새와 히위 사람들과 가나안 사람들의 모든 성읍에 이르렀고, 유다의 네겝, 곧 브엘세바로 나갔다.
ko.B: 그들은 두로 요새와 히위 사람들과 가나안 사람들의 모든 성읍에 갔다가, 유다의 네겝 지방 브엘세바로 나갔다.
ko.R: 그들은 성벽으로 둘러싸인 두로 성과 히위 사람들과 가나안 사람들이 사는 모든 마을에 갔다. 그다음에 남쪽으로 내려가 유다의 메마른 남쪽 땅인 네겝으로 가서 브엘세바에 이르렀다.

pt.L: E foram à fortaleza de Tiro e a todas as cidades dos heveus e dos cananeus, e saíram para o Neguebe de Judá, a Berseba.
pt.B: Foram à fortaleza de Tiro e a todas as cidades dos heveus e dos cananeus, e depois saíram para o Neguebe de Judá, em Berseba.
pt.R: Foram à cidade murada de Tiro e a todas as cidades onde moravam heveus e cananeus. Depois foram para o sul, até o Neguebe, a terra seca do sul de Judá, e chegaram a Berseba.

decisions.choice: the fortress of Tyre: the fortified city on Israel's northwest border
decisions.reason: Joshua 19:29 also speaks of "the fortified city of Tyre" as a point on Asher's border. The counters reached the edge of Tyre's land, not the island city itself.

decisions.choice: the Hivites and the Canaanites: older peoples still living in towns within Israel
decisions.reason: Some towns of these peoples remained inside Israel's land (Joshua 9:7; Judges 1:27-33; 1 Kings 9:20-21). They too were included in the count. The Hebrew uses the singular for each people, as a group name.

decisions.choice: the Negev of Judah, Beersheba: the dry south, at the southern limit of the land
decisions.reason: The Negev is the dry land in the south of Judah. Beersheba, its chief town, marks the southern end of the route (verse 2).

decisions.choice: walled city; the dry southern land of Judah
decisions.reason: Readable uses plain words for "fortress" and explains the name Negev.

source.text: וַיָּשֻׁ֖טוּ בְּכָל־הָאָ֑רֶץ וַיָּבֹ֜אוּ מִקְצֵ֨ה תִשְׁעָ֧ה חֳדָשִׁ֛ים וְעֶשְׂרִ֥ים י֖וֹם יְרוּשָׁלִָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And they went about through all the land, and came at [the] end of nine months and twenty days [to] Jerusalem.

en.L: And they went about through all the land, and they came to Jerusalem at the end of nine months and twenty days.
en.B: When they had gone through the whole land, they came back to Jerusalem at the end of nine months and twenty days.
en.R: They traveled through the whole country. After nine months and twenty days they came back to Jerusalem.

es.L: Y recorrieron toda la tierra, y llegaron a Jerusalén al cabo de nueve meses y veinte días.
es.B: Después de recorrer todo el país, volvieron a Jerusalén al cabo de nueve meses y veinte días.
es.R: Viajaron por todo el país. Después de nueve meses y veinte días volvieron a Jerusalén.

fr.L: Et ils parcoururent tout le pays, et ils arrivèrent à Jérusalem au bout de neuf mois et vingt jours.
fr.B: Après avoir parcouru tout le pays, ils revinrent à Jérusalem au bout de neuf mois et vingt jours.
fr.R: Ils ont voyagé dans tout le pays. Après neuf mois et vingt jours, ils sont revenus à Jérusalem.

sw.L: Wakazunguka katika nchi yote, wakafika Yerusalemu mwisho wa miezi tisa na siku ishirini.
sw.B: Walipokwisha kupita katika nchi yote, wakarudi Yerusalemu mwisho wa miezi tisa na siku ishirini.
sw.R: Wakasafiri katika nchi yote. Baada ya miezi tisa na siku ishirini wakarudi Yerusalemu.

vi.L: Họ đi khắp xứ, và sau chín tháng hai mươi ngày thì về đến Giê-ru-sa-lem.
vi.B: Sau khi đi khắp xứ, họ trở về Giê-ru-sa-lem vào cuối chín tháng hai mươi ngày.
vi.R: Họ đi khắp cả nước. Sau chín tháng hai mươi ngày, họ trở về Giê-ru-sa-lem.

ko.L: 그들은 온 땅을 두루 다니고, 아홉 달 이십 일 만에 예루살렘에 이르렀다.
ko.B: 그들은 온 땅을 두루 다닌 뒤, 아홉 달 이십 일 만에 예루살렘으로 돌아왔다.
ko.R: 그들은 온 나라를 다녔다. 그리고 아홉 달 이십 일이 지나서 예루살렘으로 돌아왔다.

pt.L: E percorreram toda a terra, e vieram a Jerusalém ao fim de nove meses e vinte dias.
pt.B: Depois de percorrerem toda a terra, voltaram a Jerusalém ao fim de nove meses e vinte dias.
pt.R: Eles viajaram pelo país inteiro. Depois de nove meses e vinte dias, voltaram para Jerusalém.

decisions.choice: went about: the same verb as David's command in verse 2
decisions.reason: The narrator repeats David's word "go about": Joab did exactly what he was told and covered the whole land.

decisions.choice: nine months and twenty days: almost ten months of work
decisions.reason: A count of every fighting man in every town was a long task. The figure shows how thorough the census was.

decisions.choice: came back
decisions.reason: They had set out from Jerusalem (verse 4), so Balanced and Readable say they came back.

source.text: וַיִּתֵּ֥ן יוֹאָ֛ב אֶת־מִסְפַּ֥ר מִפְקַד־הָעָ֖ם אֶל־הַמֶּ֑לֶךְ וַתְּהִ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֡ל שְׁמֹנֶה֩ מֵא֨וֹת אֶ֤לֶף אִֽישׁ־חַ֨יִל֙ שֹׁ֣לֵֽף חֶ֔רֶב וְאִ֣ישׁ יְהוּדָ֔ה חֲמֵשׁ־מֵא֥וֹת אֶ֖לֶף אִֽישׁ׃

records.literal_gloss: And gave Joab the number of the registration of the people to the king; and [there] was Israel eight hundred thousand men of strength drawing [the] sword, and [the] men of Judah five hundred thousand men.

en.L: And Joab gave the number of the registration of the people to the king. And Israel was 800,000 men of strength who drew the sword, and the men of Judah [were] 500,000 men.
en.B: Joab gave the king the total of the people who had been registered: in Israel there were 800,000 able-bodied men who could handle a sword, and in Judah 500,000.
en.R: Joab gave the king the results of the count. In Israel there were 800,000 strong men who could fight with a sword. In Judah there were 500,000 men.

es.L: Y Joab dio al rey el número del censo del pueblo. E Israel era 800 000 hombres fuertes que sacaban espada, y los hombres de Judá [eran] 500 000 hombres.
es.B: Joab le dio al rey el total de la gente censada: en Israel había 800 000 hombres aptos que sabían manejar la espada, y en Judá 500 000.
es.R: Joab le dio al rey el resultado del censo. En Israel había 800 000 hombres fuertes que podían pelear con espada. En Judá había 500 000 hombres.

fr.L: Et Joab donna au roi le chiffre du recensement du peuple. Et Israël était de huit cent mille hommes vaillants tirant l’épée, et les hommes de Juda [étaient] cinq cent mille hommes.
fr.B: Joab remit au roi le chiffre du recensement du peuple : il y avait en Israël huit cent mille hommes vigoureux capables de manier l’épée, et en Juda cinq cent mille.
fr.R: Joab a donné au roi les résultats du recensement. En Israël, il y avait huit cent mille hommes forts capables de se battre avec une épée. En Juda, il y en avait cinq cent mille.

sw.L: Yoabu akampa mfalme hesabu ya kuandikishwa kwa watu. Na Israeli walikuwa watu elfu mia nane wenye nguvu waliochomoa upanga, na watu wa Yuda [walikuwa] watu elfu mia tano.
sw.B: Yoabu akampa mfalme jumla ya watu walioandikishwa: katika Israeli walikuwa wanaume elfu mia nane wenye nguvu walioweza kutumia upanga, na katika Yuda elfu mia tano.
sw.R: Yoabu akampa mfalme matokeo ya hesabu. Katika Israeli walikuwa wanaume elfu mia nane wenye nguvu walioweza kupigana kwa upanga. Katika Yuda walikuwa wanaume elfu mia tano.

vi.L: Giô-áp trình lên vua con số dân đã được ghi danh: Y-sơ-ra-ên có 800.000 người mạnh mẽ cầm gươm, và người Giu-đa có 500.000 người.
vi.B: Giô-áp trình lên vua tổng số dân đã được ghi danh: Y-sơ-ra-ên có 800.000 người khỏe mạnh có thể cầm gươm, còn Giu-đa có 500.000 người.
vi.R: Giô-áp báo cho vua kết quả cuộc kiểm tra. Y-sơ-ra-ên có 800.000 người mạnh khỏe có thể cầm gươm ra trận. Giu-đa có 500.000 người.

ko.L: 요압이 등록한 백성의 수를 왕에게 보고했다. 이스라엘은 칼을 빼는 용사가 80만 명이었고, 유다 사람은 50만 명이었다.
ko.B: 요압은 등록된 백성의 총수를 왕에게 보고했다. 이스라엘에는 칼을 다룰 줄 아는 건장한 남자가 80만 명, 유다에는 50만 명이 있었다.
ko.R: 요압은 백성을 센 결과를 왕에게 보고했다. 이스라엘에는 칼을 들고 싸울 수 있는 힘센 남자가 80만 명이 있었다. 유다에는 50만 명이 있었다.

pt.L: E Joabe deu ao rei o número do recenseamento do povo. E Israel era oitocentos mil homens de força que empunhavam a espada, e os homens de Judá, quinhentos mil homens.
pt.B: Joabe entregou ao rei o total dos recenseados: em Israel havia oitocentos mil homens aptos para a guerra, que sabiam manejar a espada, e em Judá, quinhentos mil.
pt.R: Joabe deu ao rei o resultado da contagem. Em Israel havia oitocentos mil homens fortes, que podiam lutar com a espada. Em Judá havia quinhentos mil homens.

decisions.choice: 800,000 in Israel and 500,000 in Judah: the figures of this account
decisions.reason: 1 Chronicles 21:5-6, telling the same story, gives 1,100,000 for Israel and 470,000 for Judah, and adds that Joab did not count Levi and Benjamin because he found the king's order hateful. 1 Chronicles 27:24 says the count was begun but not finished. The two accounts may count different groups, or the numbers may have been changed in copying; the text does not explain the difference.

decisions.choice: thousand: the ordinary number word
decisions.reason: As in the census lists of Numbers (see the note at Numbers 1:21), the word is read here as the number "thousand", though it can also name a military or clan unit, which would give smaller numbers.

decisions.choice: men of strength who drew the sword: men fit for battle
decisions.reason: The phrase describes able-bodied men who could be called up to fight (Judges 8:10; 20:2, 17).

decisions.choice: Israel ... Judah: the two parts of David's kingdom counted separately
decisions.reason: Even under David, Israel and Judah were often named as two groups (2:4; 5:5; 19:42-44).

decisions.choice: able-bodied men who could handle a sword (Balanced); strong men who could fight with a sword (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable put the idiom in everyday words.

decisions.choice: oitocentos mil; quinhentos mil (in words)
decisions.reason: Round numbers are written in words at every level, as fixed for 1 and 2 Samuel in Portuguese (1 Samuel 24:3), where the English uses figures. "Aptos para a guerra" (B) is the phrase of Numbers 1:3 in Portuguese for men fit to fight.

source.text: וַיַּ֤ךְ לֵב־דָּוִד֙ אֹת֔וֹ אַחֲרֵי־כֵ֖ן סָפַ֣ר אֶת־הָעָ֑םסוַיֹּ֨אמֶר דָּוִ֜ד אֶל־יְהוָ֗ה חָטָ֤אתִי מְאֹד֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר עָשִׂ֔יתִי וְעַתָּ֣ה יְהוָ֔ה הַֽעֲבֶר־נָא֙ אֶת־עֲוֺ֣ן עַבְדְּךָ֔ כִּ֥י נִסְכַּ֖לְתִּי מְאֹֽד׃

records.literal_gloss: And struck [the] heart of David him after thus [that] he had counted the people. And said David to Yahweh, I have sinned greatly [in] what I have done; and now, Yahweh, take away, please, the iniquity of your servant, for I have acted foolishly exceedingly.

en.L: And David's heart struck him after he had counted the people. And David said to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, "I have sinned greatly in what I have done. And now, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, please take away the iniquity of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} servant, for I have acted very foolishly."
en.B: But after David had counted the people, his conscience struck him. David said to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, "I have sinned greatly by doing this. Now, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, please take away {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} servant's guilt, for I have acted very foolishly."
en.R: After David had counted the people, he felt guilty. He said to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, "I have done a very sinful thing. Now, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, please take away my guilt. I have been very foolish."

es.L: Y el corazón de David le golpeó después de haber contado al pueblo. Y David dijo {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}}: «He pecado gravemente en lo que he hecho. Y ahora, {{divine_name:SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, te ruego que quites la iniquidad de {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} siervo, porque he actuado muy neciamente».
es.B: Pero después de contar al pueblo, a David le remordió la conciencia. David le dijo {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}}: «He pecado gravemente al hacer esto. Ahora, {{divine_name:SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, te ruego que quites la culpa de {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} siervo, porque he actuado con mucha necedad».
es.R: Después de contar a la gente, David se sintió culpable. Le dijo {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}}: «He hecho algo muy malo. Ahora, {{divine_name:SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, por favor quítame la culpa. He sido muy necio».

fr.L: Et le cœur de David le frappa après qu’il eut dénombré le peuple. Et David dit {{divine_name:au SEIGNEUR|à Yahvé}} : « J’ai gravement péché en ce que j’ai fait. Et maintenant, {{divine_name:SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, enlève, je {{deity_pronoun:t’|T’}}en prie, la faute de {{deity_pronoun:ton|Ton}} serviteur, car j’ai agi très follement. »
fr.B: Mais après avoir dénombré le peuple, David sentit sa conscience le frapper. Il dit {{divine_name:au SEIGNEUR|à Yahvé}} : « J’ai gravement péché en agissant ainsi. Maintenant, {{divine_name:SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, je {{deity_pronoun:t’|T’}}en prie, efface la faute de {{deity_pronoun:ton|Ton}} serviteur, car j’ai agi comme un insensé. »
fr.R: Après avoir compté le peuple, David s’est senti coupable. Il a dit {{divine_name:au SEIGNEUR|à Yahvé}} : « J’ai commis un grand péché. Maintenant, {{divine_name:SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, s’il {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} plaît, enlève ma faute. J’ai été très bête. »

sw.L: Moyo wa Daudi ukampiga baada ya kuwahesabu watu. Daudi akamwambia {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, "Nimetenda dhambi kubwa katika jambo nililolifanya. Na sasa, Ee {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, tafadhali uondoe uovu wa mtumishi {{deity_pronoun:wako|Wako}}, kwa maana nimetenda kwa upumbavu sana."
sw.B: Lakini baada ya Daudi kuwahesabu watu, dhamiri yake ikamshtaki. Daudi akamwambia {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, "Nimetenda dhambi kubwa kwa kufanya hivi. Sasa, Ee {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, tafadhali uondoe hatia ya mtumishi {{deity_pronoun:wako|Wako}}, kwa maana nimetenda kwa upumbavu sana."
sw.R: Daudi alipokwisha kuwahesabu watu, akajiona mwenye hatia. Akamwambia {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, "Nimetenda dhambi kubwa sana. Sasa, Ee {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, tafadhali niondolee hatia yangu. Nimekuwa mpumbavu sana."

vi.L: Sau khi kiểm tra dân số, lòng Đa-vít đánh ông. Đa-vít thưa với {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}: "Con đã phạm tội nặng trong việc con đã làm. Bây giờ, lạy {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, xin cất bỏ tội lỗi của đầy tớ {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, vì con đã hành động rất dại dột."
vi.B: Nhưng sau khi kiểm tra dân số, Đa-vít bị lương tâm cắn rứt. Đa-vít thưa với {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}: "Con đã phạm tội nặng khi làm việc này. Bây giờ, lạy {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, xin tha tội cho đầy tớ {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, vì con đã hành động rất dại dột."
vi.R: Sau khi đếm dân, Đa-vít cảm thấy mình có tội. Ông thưa với {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}: "Con đã làm một việc rất tội lỗi. Bây giờ, lạy {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, xin tha tội cho con. Con đã quá dại dột."

ko.L: 다윗이 백성을 센 뒤에 다윗의 마음이 그를 쳤다. 다윗이 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께 아뢰었다. "제가 이 일을 하여 큰 죄를 지었습니다. 이제 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}여, 부디 주님의 종의 죄악을 없애 주십시오. 제가 너무나 어리석은 짓을 했습니다."
ko.B: 그러나 다윗은 백성을 센 뒤에 양심의 가책을 느꼈다. 다윗이 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께 아뢰었다. "제가 이 일로 큰 죄를 지었습니다. 이제 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}여, 주님의 종의 죄를 없애 주십시오. 제가 너무나 어리석은 짓을 했습니다."
ko.R: 백성을 센 뒤에 다윗은 죄책감을 느꼈다. 다윗이 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께 아뢰었다. "제가 아주 큰 죄를 지었습니다. 이제 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}여, 제 죄를 없애 주십시오. 제가 너무 어리석었습니다."

pt.L: E o coração de Davi o golpeou depois que ele contou o povo. E Davi disse {{divine_name:ao SENHOR|a Javé}}: "Pequei muito no que fiz. E agora, {{divine_name:SENHOR|Javé}}, tira, por favor, a iniquidade do {{deity_pronoun:teu|Teu}} servo, pois agi muito insensatamente."
pt.B: Mas, depois de contar o povo, Davi sentiu a consciência acusá-lo. Davi disse {{divine_name:ao SENHOR|a Javé}}: "Pequei gravemente com o que fiz. Agora, {{divine_name:SENHOR|Javé}}, por favor, tira a culpa do {{deity_pronoun:teu|Teu}} servo, pois agi como um grande insensato."
pt.R: Depois de contar o povo, Davi se sentiu culpado. Ele disse {{divine_name:ao SENHOR|a Javé}}: "Fiz uma coisa muito errada. Agora, {{divine_name:SENHOR|Javé}}, por favor, tira a minha culpa. Fui muito tolo."

decisions.choice: David's heart struck him: his conscience troubled him
decisions.reason: The same expression is used when David cut off part of Saul's robe (1 Samuel 24:6). David's own heart accuses him, before any prophet speaks.

decisions.choice: take away the iniquity: remove the guilt and its punishment
decisions.reason: The word for iniquity covers both the wrong and the guilt it brings. David asks Yahweh to remove it, as Nathan said Yahweh had "put away" his sin in 12:13, with the same verb.

decisions.choice: acted foolishly: acted against what is right, without sense
decisions.reason: The verb is used of Saul's disobedience in 1 Samuel 13:13. It is a moral failure, not merely a mistake.

decisions.choice: your servant: a humble way of saying "I"
decisions.reason: Speaking to a superior, a person called himself "your servant" (as in 7:19-29).

decisions.choice: your servant (Literal, Balanced); my (Readable)
decisions.reason: Literal and Balanced keep the polite form; Readable says "my guilt", which is what it means.

decisions.choice: his conscience struck him (Balanced); he felt guilty (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable explain the picture of the heart striking.

decisions.choice: "ton serviteur" (L, B); "ma" (R)
decisions.reason: David speaking of himself to God: "serviteur" at every level where the Hebrew has it, as the Psalms note sets for the psalmist’s "your servant"; Readable says "my", as the English does.

decisions.choice: David prays as "con" and calls himself "đầy tớ Ngài" (L, B)
decisions.reason: As the Genesis note sets for people speaking to God; Readable says "con" for "your servant", as the English says "my".

decisions.choice: David prays in the formal style (합쇼체), calling himself "주님의 종" (L, B) and "저" (R)
decisions.reason: People speak to God in prayer forms in this translation; "your servant" before God is "주님의 종", as in the Psalms.

decisions.choice: o coração de Davi o golpeou (L), a consciência o acusou (B), se sentiu culpado (R); tira; insensato
decisions.reason: The words of 1 Samuel 24:6 in Portuguese, level by level, where the same expression is used (m1); "tira", the verb Nathan uses in 12:13 in Portuguese ("tirou o seu pecado"), as the Hebrew uses the same verb (m2); and "insensato", the word of Saul's folly in 1 Samuel 13:13 (m3). David prays with "tu", and the span goes on "teu" in "o teu servo".

decisions.choice: and the word of Yahweh came: at the same time, or already
decisions.reason: The clause puts its subject first instead of the usual narrative verb form. That marks it as background to David's rising: by the time David got up, Yahweh had already spoken to Gad.

decisions.choice: Gad the prophet, David's seer: a prophet who served at David's court
decisions.reason: Gad first appears with David in his years as a fugitive (1 Samuel 22:5), and 1 Chronicles 29:29 names him among those who recorded David's history. "Seer" is an older title for a prophet, one to whom God shows things (1 Samuel 9:9 uses a related word).

decisions.choice: a prophet who brought David messages from God; the LORD said to Gad
decisions.reason: Readable explains "seer" the first time it appears in this chapter and names the speaker of the next verse.

decisions.choice: a colon in place of "saying"
decisions.reason: Balanced introduces the message with a colon, since the message begins in the next verse.

decisions.choice: Gad el profeta, el vidente de David
decisions.reason: El profeta and el vidente as the terms note; Gad is the usual Spanish form of the prophet's name, the same as the tribe's.

decisions.choice: Gadi nabii, mwonaji wa Daudi
decisions.reason: Gad has the same Swahili form as the tribe of Gad; prophet and seer are "nabii" and "mwonaji", as the Samuel terms note sets.

decisions.choice: "nhà tiên tri Gát, nhà tiên kiến của Đa-vít"
decisions.reason: As the Samuel terms note gives prophet and seer; the prophet Gad takes the same form as the tribe, as in the Vietnamese tradition.

decisions.choice: Gade, o profeta; o vidente de Davi
decisions.reason: "Gade" as 1 Samuel 22:5 in Portuguese, and "vidente", the word of 1 Samuel 9:9, formed from "ver" as the title is from "see" (m2); Readable explains it, as the English does.
