records.literal_gloss: Go and speak to David, Thus says Yahweh: Three [things] I [am] laying on you; choose for yourself one of them, and I will do [it] to you.

en.L: "Go and speak to David, 'Thus says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}: Three [things] I am laying on you. Choose for yourself one of them, and I will do [it] to you.'"
en.B: "Go and tell David, '{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} says this: I am setting three things before you. Choose one of them, and I will do it to you.'"
en.R: "Go and tell David, 'This is what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} says: I am giving you three choices. Choose one of them, and I will do it to you.'"

es.L: «Ve y di a David: “Así dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}: Tres [cosas] pongo delante de ti. Escoge para ti una de ellas, y te la haré”».
es.B: «Ve y dile a David: “{{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} dice esto: Pongo delante de ti tres cosas. Escoge una de ellas, y eso te haré”».
es.R: «Ve y dile a David: “Esto es lo que dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}: Te doy tres opciones. Escoge una de ellas, y eso te haré”».

fr.L: « Va et dis à David : “Ainsi parle {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} : Je mets trois [choses] sur toi. Choisis-toi l’une d’elles, et je te la ferai.” »
fr.B: « Va dire à David : “Voici ce que dit {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} : Je te propose trois choses. Choisis-en une, et c’est celle-là que je t’infligerai.” »
fr.R: « Va dire à David : “Voici ce que dit {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} : Je te donne trois choix. Choisis-en un, et c’est ce que je te ferai.” »

sw.L: "Nenda useme na Daudi, '{{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} asema hivi: Mambo matatu nakuwekea. Ujichagulie moja wapo, nami nitakutendea [hilo].'"
sw.B: "Nenda ukamwambie Daudi, 'Hivi ndivyo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} asemavyo: Ninaweka mambo matatu mbele yako. Chagua moja wapo, nami nitakutendea hilo.'"
sw.R: "Nenda ukamwambie Daudi, 'Hili ndilo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} analosema: Ninakupa njia tatu za kuchagua. Chagua moja wapo, nami nitakutendea hilo.'"

vi.L: "Hãy đi nói với Đa-vít: '{{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phán như vầy: Ta đặt trên ngươi ba [điều]. Hãy chọn cho mình một trong ba điều ấy, và Ta sẽ làm [điều đó] cho ngươi.'"
vi.B: "Hãy đi nói với Đa-vít: '{{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phán thế này: Ta đặt trước mặt ngươi ba điều. Hãy chọn một trong ba, và Ta sẽ làm điều đó cho ngươi.'"
vi.R: "Hãy đi nói với Đa-vít: 'Đây là điều {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phán: Ta cho ngươi ba điều để chọn. Hãy chọn một, và Ta sẽ làm điều đó cho ngươi.'"

ko.L: "가서 다윗에게 말하여라. '{{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 이렇게 말씀하신다. 내가 너에게 세 가지를 내놓는다. 너는 그 가운데 하나를 골라라. 내가 그것을 너에게 행하겠다.'"
ko.B: "가서 다윗에게 전하여라. '{{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 이렇게 말씀하신다. 내가 네 앞에 세 가지를 내놓으니, 그 가운데 하나를 골라라. 내가 그것을 너에게 내리겠다.'"
ko.R: "가서 다윗에게 전하여라. '{{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 이렇게 말씀하신다. 내가 너에게 세 가지 가운데 하나를 고르게 하겠다. 하나를 골라라. 그러면 내가 그것을 너에게 내리겠다.'"

pt.L: "Vai e fala a Davi: 'Assim diz {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}}: Três [coisas] eu ponho sobre ti. Escolhe para ti uma delas, e eu a farei contigo.'"
pt.B: "Vai dizer a Davi: '{{divine_name:O SENHOR|Javé}} diz isto: Ponho diante de ti três coisas. Escolhe uma delas, e eu a farei contigo.'"
pt.R: "Vai falar com Davi: 'Isto é o que {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} diz: Eu te dou três escolhas. Escolhe uma delas, e eu a farei contigo.'"

decisions.choice: laying on you: putting before you as a burden to choose from
decisions.reason: The verb means to lift or lay something on someone (Lamentations 3:28). The three things are all punishments; David may choose which one he will bear. 1 Chronicles 21:10 has a similar verb meaning "hold out, offer".

decisions.choice: choose one of them: the punishment is certain, its form is left to David
decisions.reason: Yahweh does not let the sin pass, but he lets David choose how the punishment will come.

decisions.choice: double quotes for Yahweh's words to Gad, single quotes for the message to David
decisions.reason: Gad is to pass on Yahweh's words, so they stand as a quotation inside Yahweh's own speech.

decisions.choice: setting three things before you (Balanced); giving you three choices (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable state the sense of "laying three on you" in natural English.

decisions.choice: "Ainsi parle le SEIGNEUR" (L); "Voici ce que dit le SEIGNEUR" (B, R)
decisions.reason: The prophetic formula *koh amar YHWH* at each level, after the English "Thus says" / "says this" / "This is what ... says". French « » for God’s words to Gad and “ ” for the message to David.
As the English, the LORD's words to Gad take the outer quotation marks and the message to David the inner ones, in the Spanish order of marks.

decisions.choice: the messenger formula "{{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 이렇게 말씀하신다" with the honorific, and God's own words in the plain style with "나" and "너"
decisions.reason: Gad will speak the opening words to David as God's messenger, so they take the honorific; the message itself is God speaking, in the plain style the terms of this translation set for him.

decisions.choice: God says "Ta" and calls David "ngươi" at every level
decisions.reason: God's words to the king he is punishing for the census keep "ngươi" at every level, as in 12:7 (5:2).

decisions.choice: tu (the LORD to Gad and to David)
decisions.reason: The LORD speaks to Gad and, through him, to David as to one person, with "tu" ("Vai", "ti", "Escolhe"), as God addresses one person throughout the Portuguese Old Testament; Gad then speaks to the king in his own words with "você" (verse 13).

source.text: וַיָּבֹא־גָ֥ד אֶל־דָּוִ֖ד וַיַּגֶּד־ל֑וֹ וַיֹּ֣אמֶר ל֡וֹ הֲתָב֣וֹא לְךָ֣ שֶֽׁבַע שָׁנִ֣ים׀רָעָ֣ב׀בְּאַרְצֶ֡ךָ אִם־שְׁלֹשָׁ֣ה חֳ֠דָשִׁים נֻסְךָ֨לִפְנֵֽי־צָרֶ֜יךָ וְה֣וּא רֹדְפֶ֗ךָ וְאִם־הֱ֠יוֹת שְׁלֹ֨שֶׁת יָמִ֥ים דֶּ֨בֶר֙ בְּאַרְצֶ֔ךָ עַתָּה֙ דַּ֣ע וּרְאֵ֔ה מָה־אָשִׁ֥יב שֹׁלְחִ֖י דָּבָֽר׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And came Gad to David and told him, and said to him, Shall come to you seven years [of] famine in your land? Or three months [of] your fleeing before your foes, and he pursuing you? Or [shall there] be three days [of] pestilence in your land? Now know and see what I shall return [to the one] sending me [as a] word.

en.L: So Gad came to David and told him, and said to him, "Shall seven years of famine come to you in your land? Or three months of your fleeing before your foes while they pursue you? Or shall there be three days of pestilence in your land? Now know and see what word I shall return to the one who sent me."
en.B: So Gad went to David and told him, "Shall seven years of famine come on your land? Or three months of running from your enemies while they chase you? Or three days of plague in your land? Now think it over and decide what answer I should take back to the one who sent me."
en.R: So Gad went to David and told him what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had said. "Which will it be? Seven years of famine in your land? Three months of running away from your enemies while they chase you? Or three days of a deadly plague in your land? Think about it and decide. Then tell me what answer I should give to the one who sent me."

es.L: Así que Gad vino a David y se lo hizo saber, y le dijo: «¿Vendrán sobre ti siete años de hambre en tu tierra? ¿O tres meses de huir tú delante de tus adversarios mientras ellos te persiguen? ¿O habrá tres días de peste en tu tierra? Ahora piensa y mira qué palabra he de llevar al que me envió».
es.B: Entonces Gad fue a David y le dijo: «¿Quieres que vengan siete años de hambre sobre tu tierra? ¿O tres meses huyendo de tus enemigos mientras ellos te persiguen? ¿O tres días de peste en tu tierra? Ahora piénsalo y decide qué respuesta debo llevarle al que me envió».
es.R: Así que Gad fue a David y le dijo lo que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} había dicho. «¿Qué escoges? ¿Siete años de hambre en tu tierra? ¿Tres meses huyendo de tus enemigos mientras ellos te persiguen? ¿O tres días de una peste mortal en tu tierra? Piénsalo y decide. Luego dime qué respuesta le debo dar al que me envió».

fr.L: Et Gad vint vers David et le lui annonça, et lui dit : « Viendra-t-il sur toi sept années de famine dans ton pays ? Ou trois mois où tu fuiras devant tes ennemis pendant qu’ils te poursuivront ? Ou y aura-t-il trois jours de peste dans ton pays ? Maintenant, sache et vois quelle parole je dois rapporter à celui qui m’a envoyé. »
fr.B: Gad se rendit donc auprès de David et lui transmit le message : « Faut-il que sept années de famine viennent sur ton pays ? Ou trois mois de fuite devant tes ennemis, pendant qu’ils te poursuivront ? Ou trois jours de peste dans ton pays ? Réfléchis maintenant et vois quelle réponse je dois rapporter à celui qui m’a envoyé. »
fr.R: Gad est donc allé voir David et lui a dit ce que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} avait dit. « Que choisis-tu ? Sept années de famine dans ton pays ? Trois mois pendant lesquels tu fuiras devant tes ennemis qui te poursuivront ? Ou trois jours d’une peste mortelle dans ton pays ? Réfléchis et décide-toi. Ensuite, dis-moi quelle réponse je dois donner à celui qui m’a envoyé. »

sw.L: Gadi akaja kwa Daudi akamwambia, akamwuliza, "Je, ikujie miaka saba ya njaa katika nchi yako? Au miezi mitatu ya kukimbia mbele ya adui zako wakikufuatia? Au iwe siku tatu za tauni katika nchi yako? Basi sasa jua na uone ni neno gani nimrudishie yule aliyenituma."
sw.B: Basi Gadi akaenda kwa Daudi akamwambia, "Je, iijie nchi yako miaka saba ya njaa? Au miezi mitatu ya kuwakimbia adui zako wakikufukuza? Au siku tatu za tauni katika nchi yako? Sasa fikiri uamue jibu nitakalompelekea yule aliyenituma."
sw.R: Basi Gadi akaenda kwa Daudi akamwambia yale {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} aliyosema. "Utachagua lipi? Miaka saba ya njaa katika nchi yako? Miezi mitatu ya kuwakimbia adui zako wakikufukuza? Au siku tatu za tauni ya kuua katika nchi yako? Fikiri uamue. Kisha uniambie jibu nitakalompa yule aliyenituma."

vi.L: Vậy Gát đến gặp Đa-vít, báo cho vua và nói: "Vua muốn bảy năm đói kém đến trên xứ của vua? Hay ba tháng vua phải chạy trốn trước mặt kẻ thù trong khi chúng đuổi theo vua? Hay ba ngày dịch bệnh trong xứ của vua? Bây giờ xin vua hãy biết và xem tôi phải đem lời nào về trả lời Đấng đã sai tôi."
vi.B: Vậy Gát đến gặp Đa-vít và thưa: "Bệ hạ muốn bảy năm đói kém xảy đến trên xứ? Hay ba tháng bệ hạ phải chạy trốn kẻ thù trong khi chúng đuổi theo? Hay ba ngày dịch lệ trong xứ? Bây giờ xin bệ hạ suy nghĩ và quyết định tôi phải đem câu trả lời nào về cho Đấng đã sai tôi."
vi.R: Vậy Gát đến gặp Đa-vít và báo cho vua những điều {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đã phán. "Đức vua chọn điều nào? Bảy năm đói kém trong xứ? Ba tháng chạy trốn kẻ thù trong khi chúng đuổi theo đức vua? Hay ba ngày bệnh dịch chết người trong xứ? Xin đức vua suy nghĩ và quyết định. Rồi cho tôi biết tôi phải trả lời thế nào với Đấng đã sai tôi."

ko.L: 갓이 다윗에게 가서 그에게 알리며 말했다. "임금님의 땅에 일곱 해 동안 기근이 임하게 하시겠습니까? 아니면 임금님께서 원수들 앞에서 석 달 동안 도망 다니시고 그들이 임금님을 뒤쫓게 하시겠습니까? 아니면 임금님의 땅에 사흘 동안 전염병이 돌게 하시겠습니까? 이제 저를 보내신 분께 제가 무슨 대답을 가지고 돌아가야 할지 잘 생각해 보십시오."
ko.B: 그래서 갓이 다윗에게 가서 말했다. "임금님의 땅에 일곱 해 동안 기근이 들게 하시겠습니까? 아니면 석 달 동안 원수들에게 쫓겨 다니시겠습니까? 아니면 임금님의 땅에 사흘 동안 전염병이 돌게 하시겠습니까? 이제 잘 생각하셔서, 저를 보내신 분께 제가 어떤 대답을 가지고 가야 할지 정해 주십시오."
ko.R: 그래서 갓이 다윗에게 가서 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 하신 말씀을 전했다. "어느 것을 고르시겠습니까? 임금님의 땅에 일곱 해 동안 기근이 드는 것입니까? 석 달 동안 원수들에게 쫓겨 도망 다니시는 것입니까? 아니면 임금님의 땅에 사흘 동안 무서운 전염병이 도는 것입니까? 잘 생각해서 정하십시오. 그리고 저를 보내신 분께 제가 무슨 대답을 드려야 할지 말씀해 주십시오."

pt.L: E Gade veio a Davi, e lhe anunciou, e lhe disse: "Virão sobre você sete anos de fome na sua terra? Ou três meses de você fugir diante dos seus adversários, enquanto eles o perseguem? Ou haverá três dias de peste na sua terra? Agora saiba e veja que palavra devo levar de volta a quem me enviou."
pt.B: Então Gade foi até Davi e lhe disse: "Virão sete anos de fome sobre a sua terra? Ou três meses fugindo dos seus inimigos, enquanto eles o perseguem? Ou três dias de peste na sua terra? Agora pense bem e decida que resposta devo levar a quem me enviou."
pt.R: Então Gade foi até Davi e lhe contou o que {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} tinha dito. "Qual vai ser? Sete anos de fome na sua terra? Três meses fugindo dos seus inimigos, enquanto eles o perseguem? Ou três dias de uma peste mortal na sua terra? Pense nisso e decida. Depois me diga que resposta devo dar a quem me enviou."

decisions.choice: seven years: the reading of the Hebrew text of Samuel
decisions.reason: 1 Chronicles 21:12, in the same story, reads "three years", and so does the ancient Greek translation of this verse. Three would match the pattern of the offer: three years, three months, three days. The Hebrew of Samuel reads seven, and is kept here; the difference may have arisen in copying.

decisions.choice: pestilence: a deadly epidemic sent as a judgment
decisions.reason: The word names a sudden, widespread deadly disease. In the law it is one of the judgments for breaking the covenant (Leviticus 26:25; Numbers 14:12; Deuteronomy 28:21).

decisions.choice: while he pursues you: the enemy as a whole
decisions.reason: The pronoun is singular, standing for the whole body of enemies, so it is given as "they".

decisions.choice: know and see: consider and decide
decisions.reason: The pair of verbs asks David to think the matter through and make his choice (1 Samuel 25:17).

decisions.choice: they pursue you; they chase you
decisions.reason: English uses the plural for the enemy as a group; a singular "he" could be taken for Yahweh.

decisions.choice: plague (Balanced); deadly plague (Readable)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "pestilence" for this word and "plague" for the different word in verses 21 and 25; Balanced and Readable use the everyday word "plague" for both.

decisions.choice: told him what the LORD had said; Which will it be?
decisions.reason: Readable says what Gad told David and adds a question that introduces the three choices.

decisions.choice: Gad says "vua" / "bệ hạ" / "đức vua" and "tôi" to David
decisions.reason: The prophet speaks to David with the court forms, as Nathan does; God's own words to David are given in verse 12.

decisions.choice: Gad speaks to David in the formal style (합쇼체) with "임금님"; David answers the prophet in the semi-formal style (하오체)
decisions.reason: The prophet addresses his king with court courtesy; the king, speaking to the man who brings him God's word, uses the semi-formal style rather than the plain style he uses to his officials.

decisions.choice: a peste (deber, verses 13, 15); a praga (maggefah, verses 21, 25)
decisions.reason: Portuguese keeps the two Hebrew words apart at every level: "peste" is the everyday word for a deadly epidemic (m2), and "praga" the word of Numbers 17:13-15 in Portuguese for the blow that is stopped; the English Balanced and Readable say "plague" for both. Gad speaks to the king with "você", as the prophet does in 1 Samuel 22:5.

source.text: וַיֹּ֧אמֶר דָּוִ֛ד אֶל־גָּ֖ד צַר־לִ֣י מְאֹ֑ד נִפְּלָה־נָּ֤א בְיַד־יְהוָה֙ כִּֽי־רַבִּ֣ים רַֽחֲמָ֔יו וּבְיַד־אָדָ֖ם אַל־אֶפֹּֽלָה׃

records.literal_gloss: And said David to Gad, [It is] distress to me exceedingly. Let us fall, please, into [the] hand of Yahweh, for great [are] his mercies; but into [the] hand of man let me not fall.

en.L: And David said to Gad, "[It is] very distressing to me. Let us fall, please, into the hand of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, for {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} mercies [are] great; but into the hand of man let me not fall."
en.B: David said to Gad, "I am in deep distress. Let us fall into the hand of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, for {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} mercy is great; but do not let me fall into human hands."
en.R: David answered Gad, "This is a terrible choice! Let it be {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} who punishes us, because {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} is very merciful. But do not let me fall into the power of human beings."

es.L: Y David dijo a Gad: «[Es] muy angustioso para mí. Caigamos, te ruego, en la mano {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}, porque grandes [son] {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} misericordias; pero en la mano del hombre no caiga yo».
es.B: David le dijo a Gad: «Estoy en una gran angustia. Caigamos en la mano {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}, porque {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} misericordia es grande; pero que no caiga yo en manos humanas».
es.R: David le respondió a Gad: «¡Es una decisión terrible! Que sea {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} quien nos castigue, porque {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} es muy misericordioso. Pero que no caiga yo en el poder de los hombres».

fr.L: Et David dit à Gad : « [Je suis] dans une grande angoisse. Tombons donc entre les mains {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}}, car {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} compassions [sont] grandes ; mais que je ne tombe pas entre les mains des hommes ! »
fr.B: David dit à Gad : « Je suis dans une grande angoisse. Tombons plutôt entre les mains {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}}, car {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} compassion est grande ; mais que je ne tombe pas entre des mains humaines ! »
fr.R: David a répondu à Gad : « C’est un choix terrible ! Que ce soit {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} qui nous punisse, car {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} est plein de compassion. Mais que je ne tombe pas entre les mains des hommes. »

sw.L: Daudi akamwambia Gadi, "[Ni] dhiki kubwa kwangu. Tafadhali na tuanguke mkononi mwa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, kwa maana rehema {{deity_pronoun:zake|Zake}} [ni] nyingi; lakini nisianguke mkononi mwa mwanadamu."
sw.B: Daudi akamwambia Gadi, "Nimo katika dhiki kubwa. Na tuanguke mkononi mwa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, kwa maana rehema {{deity_pronoun:zake|Zake}} ni nyingi; lakini nisianguke mikononi mwa wanadamu."
sw.R: Daudi akamjibu Gadi, "Huu ni uchaguzi mgumu mno! Na awe {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} atakayetuadhibu, kwa sababu {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} ni mwingi wa rehema. Lakini nisianguke katika mamlaka ya wanadamu."

vi.L: Đa-vít nói với Gát: "[Thật] tôi vô cùng khốn quẫn. Xin cho chúng ta sa vào tay {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, vì lòng thương xót của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} [thì] lớn lao; nhưng xin đừng để tôi sa vào tay loài người."
vi.B: Đa-vít nói với Gát: "Tôi đang vô cùng khốn quẫn. Hãy để chúng ta sa vào tay {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, vì lòng thương xót của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} thật lớn lao; nhưng đừng để tôi sa vào tay loài người."
vi.R: Đa-vít trả lời Gát: "Thật là một sự lựa chọn khủng khiếp! Hãy để chính {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phạt chúng ta, vì {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} rất thương xót. Nhưng đừng để tôi rơi vào tay loài người."

ko.L: 다윗이 갓에게 말했다. "나는 몹시 괴롭소. 부디 우리가 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 손에 빠지게 하시오. 그분의 긍휼이 크시기 때문이오. 그러나 내가 사람의 손에는 빠지지 않게 하시오."
ko.B: 다윗이 갓에게 말했다. "참으로 괴롭소. {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 손에 우리가 빠지는 것이 낫겠소. 그분은 자비가 크신 분이시니 말이오. 그러나 사람의 손에는 내가 빠지지 않게 해 주시오."
ko.R: 다윗이 갓에게 대답했다. "참으로 어려운 선택이오! {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 우리에게 벌을 내리시게 하시오. 그분은 자비가 많으신 분이시오. 그러나 내가 사람들의 손에 넘어가지는 않게 해 주시오."

pt.L: E Davi disse a Gade: "[Estou] em grande angústia. Caiamos, por favor, na mão {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}}, pois as {{deity_pronoun:suas|Suas}} misericórdias [são] grandes; mas na mão do homem não caia eu."
pt.B: Davi respondeu a Gade: "Estou em grande angústia. Caiamos nas mãos {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}}, pois a {{deity_pronoun:sua|Sua}} misericórdia é grande; mas que eu não caia em mãos humanas."
pt.R: Davi respondeu a Gade: "Que escolha terrível! Que seja {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} quem nos castigue, porque {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} é muito misericordioso. Mas que eu não caia no poder de seres humanos."

decisions.choice: fall into the hand of: come under the power of
decisions.reason: "Hand" stands for power. David would rather be punished directly by Yahweh than be handed over to enemies.

decisions.choice: mercies: deep compassion
decisions.reason: The word is plural, for the many acts of Yahweh's compassion. It is the love of a parent for a child (Psalm 103:13).

decisions.choice: let us fall ... let me not fall: David chooses the punishment that comes straight from Yahweh
decisions.reason: David speaks for the whole people ("us") and then for himself ("me"). He refuses the three months of flight from enemies; he does not name famine or pestilence, and Yahweh sends the pestilence (verse 15).

decisions.choice: This is a terrible choice!; Let it be the LORD who punishes us
decisions.reason: Readable explains the idiom "fall into the hand of" and puts David's distress in plain words.

decisions.choice: David says "tôi" to Gad the prophet
decisions.reason: To God's prophet the king speaks as an equal, not with the royal "ta".

source.text: וַיִּתֵּ֨ן יְהוָ֥ה דֶּ֨בֶר֙ בְּיִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל מֵהַבֹּ֖קֶר וְעַד־עֵ֣ת מוֹעֵ֑ד וַיָּ֣מָת מִן־הָעָ֗ם מִדָּן֙ וְעַד־בְּאֵ֣ר שֶׁ֔בַע שִׁבְעִ֥ים אֶ֖לֶף אִֽישׁ׃

records.literal_gloss: And put Yahweh pestilence on Israel from the morning and until [the] time appointed; and died of the people from Dan and to Beer-sheba seventy thousand man.

en.L: So {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} sent pestilence on Israel from the morning until the appointed time, and of the people from Dan to Beersheba 70,000 {{gender:people|men}} died.
en.B: So {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} sent a plague on Israel from that morning until the time that had been set, and 70,000 of the people died, from Dan to Beersheba.
en.R: So {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} sent a plague on Israel. It lasted from that morning until the time that had been set. All through the land, from Dan to Beersheba, 70,000 people died.

es.L: Así que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} envió peste sobre Israel desde la mañana hasta el tiempo señalado, y murieron del pueblo, desde Dan hasta Beerseba, 70 000 {{gender:personas|hombres}}.
es.B: Así que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} envió una peste sobre Israel desde aquella mañana hasta el tiempo señalado, y murieron 70 000 personas del pueblo, desde Dan hasta Beerseba.
es.R: Así que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} envió una peste sobre Israel. Duró desde aquella mañana hasta el tiempo señalado. Por todo el país, desde Dan hasta Beerseba, murieron 70 000 personas.

fr.L: Et {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} envoya la peste sur Israël depuis le matin jusqu’au temps fixé ; et il mourut du peuple, depuis Dan jusqu’à Beer-Shéba, soixante-dix mille {{gender:personnes|hommes}}.
fr.B: {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} envoya donc la peste sur Israël, depuis ce matin-là jusqu’au moment fixé, et soixante-dix mille personnes du peuple moururent, depuis Dan jusqu’à Beer-Shéba.
fr.R: {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} a donc envoyé une peste sur Israël. Elle a duré depuis ce matin-là jusqu’au moment qui avait été fixé. Dans tout le pays, depuis Dan jusqu’à Beer-Shéba, soixante-dix mille personnes sont mortes.

sw.L: Basi {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} akaleta tauni juu ya Israeli tangu asubuhi mpaka wakati ulioamriwa, na wakafa katika watu, tangu Dani mpaka Beer-sheba, watu elfu sabini.
sw.B: Basi {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} akaleta tauni juu ya Israeli tangu asubuhi ile mpaka wakati ulioamriwa, na watu elfu sabini wakafa, tangu Dani mpaka Beer-sheba.
sw.R: Basi {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} akaleta tauni juu ya Israeli. Ilidumu tangu asubuhi ile mpaka wakati ulioamriwa. Katika nchi yote, tangu Dani mpaka Beer-sheba, watu elfu sabini walikufa.

vi.L: Vậy {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} giáng dịch bệnh trên Y-sơ-ra-ên từ buổi sáng cho đến thời điểm đã định; từ Đan đến Bê-e-Sê-ba có 70.000 người trong dân chúng chết.
vi.B: Vậy {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} giáng dịch lệ trên Y-sơ-ra-ên từ sáng hôm ấy cho đến thời điểm đã định, và từ Đan đến Bê-e-Sê-ba có 70.000 người chết.
vi.R: Vậy {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} giáng bệnh dịch trên Y-sơ-ra-ên. Bệnh dịch kéo dài từ sáng hôm ấy cho đến thời điểm đã định. Khắp cả xứ, từ Đan đến Bê-e-Sê-ba, có 70.000 người chết.

ko.L: 그리하여 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 그날 아침부터 정하신 때까지 이스라엘에 전염병을 내리셨다. 단에서 브엘세바까지 백성 가운데 7만 명이 죽었다.
ko.B: 그래서 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 그날 아침부터 정해진 때까지 이스라엘에 전염병을 내리셨다. 단에서 브엘세바까지 백성 가운데 7만 명이 죽었다.
ko.R: 그래서 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 이스라엘에 전염병을 내리셨다. 전염병은 그날 아침부터 정해진 때까지 계속되었다. 단에서 브엘세바까지 온 나라에서 7만 명이 죽었다.

pt.L: Então {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} enviou peste sobre Israel, desde a manhã até o tempo determinado, e morreram do povo, desde Dã até Berseba, setenta mil {{gender:pessoas|homens}}.
pt.B: Então {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} mandou uma peste sobre Israel, daquela manhã até o tempo marcado, e morreram setenta mil pessoas do povo, de Dã até Berseba.
pt.R: Então {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} mandou uma peste sobre Israel. Ela durou daquela manhã até o tempo marcado. Em todo o país, de Dã até Berseba, morreram setenta mil pessoas.

decisions.choice: the appointed time: the time Yahweh had set for the plague to end
alternatives: the end of the three days
decisions.reason: This may mean the end of the three days offered in verse 13. But in verse 16 Yahweh stops the plague before Jerusalem is struck, so the time set may have been shorter than three days. The text does not say which.

decisions.choice: 70,000 persons: men and women among the people
decisions.reason: The word usually meaning "man" is used here as a counting word for persons, as often after numbers. The plague struck "the people", not only the men counted in verse 9. On the number word, see verse 9.

decisions.choice: from Dan to Beersheba: through the whole land
decisions.reason: The plague reaches everywhere the census reached (verse 2).

decisions.choice: people (default); men (alternative)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew word here counts persons of both sexes, so Literal uses the gender setting.

decisions.choice: a plague
decisions.reason: As in verse 13.

decisions.choice: {{gender:personas|hombres}}
decisions.reason: As the English span: the Hebrew word 'man' here counts people; Spanish has the same two wordings, 'personas' by default and 'hombres' as the alternative.

decisions.choice: watu, no gender span
decisions.reason: "Watu" already means people of both sexes, and "wanaume" would say only men, so Swahili has no second wording for the English "people|men" span.

decisions.choice: "người" with no gender span
decisions.reason: The Hebrew counts persons of both sexes (meaning decision); Vietnamese "người" says exactly that, so there is no second wording to set.

source.text: וַיִּשְׁלַח֩ יָד֨וֹ הַמַּלְאָ֥ךְ׀יְרֽוּשָׁלִַם֮ לְשַׁחֲתָהּ֒ וַיִּנָּ֤חֶם יְהוָה֙ אֶל־הָ֣רָעָ֔ה וַ֠יֹּאמֶר לַמַּלְאָ֞ךְ הַמַּשְׁחִ֤ית בָּעָם֙ רַ֔ב עַתָּ֖ה הֶ֣רֶף יָדֶ֑ךָ וּמַלְאַ֤ךְ יְהוָה֙ הָיָ֔ה עִם־גֹּ֖רֶן הָאֲרַ֥וְנָה הַיְבֻסִֽי׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And stretched out his hand the angel [to] Jerusalem to destroy it, and relented Yahweh concerning the harm, and said to the angel destroying among the people, Enough! Now let drop your hand. And [the] angel of Yahweh was by [the] threshing floor of the Araunah the Jebusite.

en.L: And the angel stretched out his hand toward Jerusalem to destroy it, and {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} relented concerning the harm, and said to the angel who was destroying among the people, "Enough! Now let your hand drop." And the angel of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} was by the threshing floor of Araunah the Jebusite.
en.B: But as the angel reached out his hand toward Jerusalem to destroy it, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} relented from the disaster. He said to the angel who was bringing destruction on the people, "Enough! Now hold back your hand." The angel of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} was then by the threshing floor of Araunah the Jebusite.
en.R: The angel reached out his hand to destroy Jerusalem. But {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} was sorry for the harm being done, so {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} decided to stop it. He said to the angel who was killing the people, "That is enough! Stop now!" At that moment the angel of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} was beside the threshing floor of Araunah the Jebusite. A threshing floor was a flat, open place where grain was beaten out.

es.L: Y el ángel extendió su mano hacia Jerusalén para destruirla, y {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} se arrepintió del mal, y dijo al ángel que destruía al pueblo: «¡Basta! Ahora retira tu mano». Y el ángel {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} estaba junto a la era de Arauna el jebuseo.
es.B: Pero cuando el ángel extendió la mano hacia Jerusalén para destruirla, {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} se arrepintió del castigo. Le dijo al ángel que traía destrucción sobre el pueblo: «¡Basta! Detén ya tu mano». El ángel {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} estaba entonces junto a la era de Arauna el jebuseo.
es.R: El ángel extendió la mano para destruir Jerusalén. Pero {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} sintió pena por el mal que se estaba haciendo, así que {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} decidió detenerlo. Le dijo al ángel que estaba matando a la gente: «¡Ya basta! ¡Detente!». En ese momento el ángel {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} estaba junto a la era de Arauna el jebuseo. Una era era un lugar plano y abierto donde se trillaba el grano.

fr.L: Et l’ange étendit sa main vers Jérusalem pour la détruire ; et {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} se repentit du mal, et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} dit à l’ange qui détruisait parmi le peuple : « Assez ! Maintenant, retire ta main. » Et l’ange {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} était près de l’aire d’Aravna le Jébusien.
fr.B: Mais au moment où l’ange étendait la main vers Jérusalem pour la détruire, {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} renonça au malheur. Il dit à l’ange qui frappait le peuple : « Assez ! Retiens maintenant ta main. » L’ange {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} se trouvait alors près de l’aire d’Aravna le Jébusien.
fr.R: L’ange a tendu la main pour détruire Jérusalem. Mais {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} a eu de la peine pour le mal qui était fait, et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} a décidé de l’arrêter. Il a dit à l’ange qui tuait les gens : « Ça suffit ! Arrête maintenant ! » À ce moment-là, l’ange {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} était à côté de l’aire d’Aravna le Jébusien. Une aire était un endroit plat et dégagé où l’on battait les céréales pour en séparer les grains.

sw.L: Malaika akanyosha mkono wake juu ya Yerusalemu ili auangamize, naye {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} akaghairi kuhusu mabaya hayo, akamwambia malaika aliyekuwa akiwaangamiza watu, "Inatosha! Sasa ushushe mkono wako." Na malaika wa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alikuwa karibu na uwanja wa kupuria wa Arauna Myebusi.
sw.B: Lakini malaika alipounyosha mkono wake kuelekea Yerusalemu ili kuuangamiza, {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} akaghairi kuleta maafa hayo. Akamwambia malaika aliyekuwa akiwaangamiza watu, "Inatosha! Sasa zuia mkono wako." Wakati huo malaika wa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alikuwa karibu na uwanja wa kupuria wa Arauna Myebusi.
sw.R: Malaika akanyosha mkono wake ili kuuangamiza Yerusalemu. Lakini {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} akasikitika kwa madhara yaliyokuwa yakitendeka, akaamua kuyakomesha. Akamwambia malaika aliyekuwa akiwaua watu, "Inatosha! Acha sasa!" Wakati huo malaika wa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alikuwa kando ya uwanja wa kupuria wa Arauna Myebusi. Uwanja wa kupuria ulikuwa mahali pa wazi palipo sawa ambapo nafaka ilipigwa ili kutenganishwa na makapi.

vi.L: Thiên sứ đưa tay ra hướng về Giê-ru-sa-lem để hủy diệt thành, thì {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đổi ý về tai họa ấy, và phán với thiên sứ đang hủy diệt dân chúng: "Đủ rồi! Bây giờ hãy hạ tay xuống." Lúc ấy thiên sứ của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đang ở bên sân đập lúa của A-rau-na người Giê-bu-sít.
vi.B: Nhưng khi thiên sứ đưa tay ra hướng về Giê-ru-sa-lem để hủy diệt thành, {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đổi ý không giáng tai họa nữa. Ngài phán với thiên sứ đang hủy diệt dân chúng: "Đủ rồi! Bây giờ hãy rút tay lại." Lúc ấy thiên sứ của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đang ở bên sân đập lúa của A-rau-na người Giê-bu-sít.
vi.R: Thiên sứ đưa tay ra để hủy diệt Giê-ru-sa-lem. Nhưng {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} thương xót vì tai họa đang xảy ra, nên {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} quyết định dừng lại. Ngài phán với thiên sứ đang giết dân chúng: "Đủ rồi! Dừng lại ngay!" Lúc ấy thiên sứ của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đang ở bên sân đập lúa của A-rau-na người Giê-bu-sít. Sân đập lúa là một khoảng đất bằng phẳng, trống trải, nơi người ta đập lúa.

ko.L: 천사가 예루살렘을 멸하려고 그 위로 손을 뻗었을 때, {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 그 재앙에 대해 마음을 돌이키시고, 백성을 멸하는 천사에게 말씀하셨다. "됐다! 이제 네 손을 거두어라." 그때 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 천사는 여부스 사람 아라우나의 타작마당 곁에 있었다.
ko.B: 그러나 천사가 예루살렘을 멸하려고 손을 뻗었을 때, {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 그 재앙을 거두기로 마음을 바꾸셨다. 그분께서 백성을 멸하던 천사에게 말씀하셨다. "그만하면 됐다! 이제 손을 거두어라." 그때 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 천사는 여부스 사람 아라우나의 타작마당 곁에 있었다.
ko.R: 천사가 예루살렘을 멸하려고 손을 뻗었다. 그러나 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서는 백성이 당하는 재앙을 안타깝게 여기셔서 그것을 멈추기로 하셨다. 그분께서 백성을 죽이던 천사에게 말씀하셨다. "그만하면 됐다! 이제 멈추어라!" 그때 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 천사는 여부스 사람 아라우나의 타작마당 곁에 있었다. 타작마당은 곡식을 떠는 평평하고 넓은 곳이었다.

pt.L: E o anjo estendeu a sua mão sobre Jerusalém para destruí-la, e {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} voltou atrás quanto ao mal, e disse ao anjo destruidor entre o povo: "Basta! Agora retira a tua mão." E o anjo {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}} estava junto à eira de Araúna, o jebuseu.
pt.B: Mas, quando o anjo estendeu a mão contra Jerusalém para destruí-la, {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} desistiu da desgraça. Ele disse ao anjo que trazia destruição sobre o povo: "Basta! Agora recolhe a tua mão." O anjo {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}} estava então junto à eira de Araúna, o jebuseu.
pt.R: O anjo estendeu a mão para destruir Jerusalém. Mas {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} ficou com pena por causa do mal que estava sendo feito, e por isso {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} decidiu pará-lo. Ele disse ao anjo que estava matando o povo: "Já chega! Para agora!" Naquele momento o anjo {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}} estava junto à eira de Araúna, o jebuseu. A eira era um lugar plano e aberto onde se batia o cereal.

decisions.choice: Yahweh relented concerning the harm: he was moved to stop the disaster
decisions.reason: The verb means to be moved with grief or pity and so to change course (Exodus 32:14; Jeremiah 18:8). It is Yahweh's mercy, which David had trusted in (verse 14), that stops the plague, before David's prayer or offering.

decisions.choice: the angel who was destroying: Yahweh's messenger carrying out the judgment
decisions.reason: The plague is pictured as the work of an angel, as the destroyer who struck Egypt (Exodus 12:23). The angel acts only at Yahweh's command and stops when he is told.

decisions.choice: Araunah: the name as the reading tradition gives it
decisions.reason: The written Hebrew spells the name in several ways in this chapter: here with the article ("the Araunah") and a different spelling, in verse 18 differently again, and in verses 20-24 as Araunah. The traditional reading gives Araunah throughout. 1 Chronicles 21 calls him Ornan. The article may suggest that the word was once a title rather than a name, but this is not certain.

decisions.choice: the threshing floor of Araunah the Jebusite: a level place on the hill north of David's city
decisions.reason: A threshing floor was a hard, flat area, usually on high open ground where the wind carried off the chaff. The Jebusites had held Jerusalem before David took it (5:6-9). This spot became the site of the temple (2 Chronicles 3:1).

decisions.choice: was sorry for the harm being done, so he decided to stop it; A threshing floor was ...
decisions.reason: Readable explains "relented" and adds a sentence saying what a threshing floor was.

decisions.choice: Aravna le Jébusien
decisions.reason: The name as read in the Hebrew tradition (m3), in a French spelling; kept for both books.

decisions.choice: la era de Arauna el jebuseo
decisions.reason: Arauna is the usual Spanish form of the name as 2 Samuel spells it; 'la era' is the threshing floor, which Readable explains as the English does.

decisions.choice: Arauna Myebusi
decisions.reason: Araunah is not in the terms note; the name follows the usual Swahili pattern, and "the Jebusite" is "Myebusi", from Wayebusi in the terms note.

decisions.choice: "A-rau-na người Giê-bu-sít"; "sân đập lúa"
decisions.reason: The usual Vietnamese form of the name, kept in verses 18-24 whatever the spelling of the Hebrew letters (meaning decision).

decisions.choice: voltou atrás (L), desistiu (B); o anjo destruidor (L)
decisions.reason: "Voltar atrás" and "desistir" are the words of Exodus 32:14 in Portuguese for the LORD's change of course (m1); "arrepender-se" would suggest sorrow for a wrong done. Literal calls the angel "o anjo destruidor", with the participle of Exodus 12:23, where Portuguese says "o destruidor" (m2); Balanced and Readable describe what he was doing, as the English does. The LORD speaks to the angel with "tu".

decisions.choice: a eira de Araúna, o jebuseu
decisions.reason: "Araúna", with the accent its stress needs, for the name as the reading tradition gives it throughout the chapter (m3), and "o jebuseu", as the Pentateuch names the people; "eira" is the word of 1 Samuel 23:1 in Portuguese for the threshing floor (m4), which Readable explains, as the English does.

source.text: וַיֹּאמֶר֩ דָּוִ֨ד אֶל־יְהוָ֜ה בִּרְאֹת֣וֹ׀אֶֽת־הַמַּלְאָ֣ךְ׀הַמַּכֶּ֣ה בָעָ֗ם וַיֹּ֨אמֶר֙ הִנֵּ֨ה אָנֹכִ֤י חָטָ֨אתִי֙ וְאָנֹכִ֣י הֶעֱוֵ֔יתִי וְאֵ֥לֶּה הַצֹּ֖אן מֶ֣ה עָשׂ֑וּ תְּהִ֨י נָ֥א יָדְךָ֛ בִּ֖י וּבְבֵ֥ית אָבִֽי׃פ

records.literal_gloss: And said David to Yahweh when he saw the angel striking among the people, and he said, Look, I [am the one who] has sinned, and I [am the one who] has done wrong; and these, the sheep, what have they done? Let be, please, your hand against me and against [the] house of my father.

en.L: And David spoke to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} when he saw the angel who was striking the people, and he said, "Look, I [am the one who] has sinned, and I [am the one who] has done wrong; but these sheep, what have they done? Please let {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} hand be against me and against my father's house."
en.B: When David saw the angel who was striking down the people, he said to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, "I am the one who has sinned; I am the one who has done wrong. But what have these sheep done? Please let {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} hand be against me and my father's family."
en.R: David saw the angel who was killing the people. He said to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, "I am the one who sinned. I am the one who did wrong. These people are like sheep. What have they done to deserve this? Please punish me and my family instead."

es.L: Y David habló {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}} cuando vio al ángel que hería al pueblo, y dijo: «He aquí, yo [soy el que] ha pecado, y yo [soy el que] ha hecho el mal; pero estas ovejas, ¿qué han hecho? Te ruego que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} mano sea contra mí y contra la casa de mi padre».
es.B: Cuando David vio al ángel que hería al pueblo, le dijo {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}}: «Yo soy el que ha pecado; yo soy el que ha hecho el mal. Pero estas ovejas, ¿qué han hecho? Te ruego que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} mano se vuelva contra mí y contra la familia de mi padre».
es.R: David vio al ángel que estaba matando a la gente. Le dijo {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}}: «Yo soy el que pecó. Yo soy el que hizo el mal. Esta gente es como un rebaño de ovejas. ¿Qué han hecho para merecer esto? Por favor, castígame a mí y a mi familia en lugar de ellos».

fr.L: Et David parla {{divine_name:au SEIGNEUR|à Yahvé}} quand il vit l’ange qui frappait le peuple, et il dit : « Voici, c’est moi qui ai péché, et c’est moi qui ai mal agi ; mais ces brebis, qu’ont-elles fait ? Que {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} main soit donc contre moi et contre la maison de mon père ! »
fr.B: Quand David vit l’ange qui frappait le peuple, il dit {{divine_name:au SEIGNEUR|à Yahvé}} : « C’est moi qui ai péché ; c’est moi qui ai mal agi. Mais ces brebis, qu’ont-elles fait ? Que {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} main soit contre moi et contre la famille de mon père ! »
fr.R: David a vu l’ange qui tuait les gens. Il a dit {{divine_name:au SEIGNEUR|à Yahvé}} : « C’est moi qui ai péché. C’est moi qui ai mal agi. Ces gens sont comme des moutons. Qu’est-ce qu’ils ont fait pour mériter cela ? S’il {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} plaît, punis plutôt ma famille et moi. »

sw.L: Daudi akamwambia {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alipomwona malaika aliyekuwa akiwapiga watu, akasema, "Tazama, mimi [ndiye] niliyetenda dhambi, na mimi [ndiye] niliyetenda uovu; lakini kondoo hawa, wamefanya nini? Tafadhali mkono {{deity_pronoun:wako|Wako}} uwe juu yangu na juu ya nyumba ya baba yangu."
sw.B: Daudi alipomwona malaika aliyekuwa akiwapiga watu, akamwambia {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, "Mimi ndiye niliyetenda dhambi; mimi ndiye niliyekosa. Lakini kondoo hawa wamefanya nini? Tafadhali mkono {{deity_pronoun:wako|Wako}} uwe juu yangu na juu ya jamaa ya baba yangu."
sw.R: Daudi akamwona malaika aliyekuwa akiwaua watu. Akamwambia {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, "Mimi ndiye niliyetenda dhambi. Mimi ndiye niliyekosa. Watu hawa ni kama kondoo. Wamefanya nini hata wastahili haya? Tafadhali uniadhibu mimi na jamaa yangu badala yao."

vi.L: Khi thấy thiên sứ đang đánh dân chúng, Đa-vít thưa với {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}: "Kìa, chính con đã phạm tội, chính con đã làm điều sai trái; còn những con chiên này, chúng đã làm gì? Xin tay {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} hãy giáng trên con và trên nhà cha con."
vi.B: Khi thấy thiên sứ đang đánh giết dân chúng, Đa-vít thưa với {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}: "Chính con là người đã phạm tội; chính con là người đã làm điều sai trái. Nhưng những con chiên này đã làm gì? Xin tay {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} giáng trên con và gia đình cha con."
vi.R: Đa-vít thấy thiên sứ đang giết dân chúng. Ông thưa với {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}: "Chính con là người đã phạm tội. Chính con là người đã làm điều sai trái. Những người này như bầy chiên. Họ đã làm gì mà phải chịu như thế? Xin hãy phạt con và gia đình con thay cho họ."

ko.L: 다윗이 백성을 치는 천사를 보았을 때 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께 말씀드렸다. "보십시오, 죄를 지은 것은 저이고, 잘못을 저지른 것도 저입니다. 그러나 이 양 떼는 무엇을 했습니까? 부디 주님의 손으로 저와 제 아버지의 집을 치십시오."
ko.B: 다윗은 백성을 쳐 죽이는 천사를 보고 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께 아뢰었다. "죄를 지은 사람은 저입니다. 잘못을 저지른 사람도 저입니다. 그러나 이 양 떼는 무엇을 했습니까? 부디 주님의 손으로 저와 제 아버지의 집안을 치십시오."
ko.R: 다윗은 백성을 죽이는 천사를 보았다. 다윗이 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께 아뢰었다. "죄를 지은 사람은 저입니다. 잘못을 한 사람도 저입니다. 이 백성은 양 떼와 같습니다. 그들이 무슨 잘못을 해서 이런 벌을 받아야 합니까? 부디 그들 대신 저와 제 집안에 벌을 내려 주십시오."

pt.L: E Davi falou {{divine_name:ao SENHOR|a Javé}} quando viu o anjo que feria o povo, e disse: "Eis que [fui] eu [que] pequei, e [fui] eu [que] agi perversamente; mas estas ovelhas, o que fizeram? Seja, por favor, a {{deity_pronoun:tua|Tua}} mão contra mim e contra a casa do meu pai."
pt.B: Quando Davi viu o anjo que estava ferindo o povo, disse {{divine_name:ao SENHOR|a Javé}}: "Fui eu que pequei; fui eu que agi mal. Mas estas ovelhas, o que fizeram? Por favor, que a {{deity_pronoun:tua|Tua}} mão seja contra mim e contra a família do meu pai."
pt.R: Davi viu o anjo que estava matando o povo. Ele disse {{divine_name:ao SENHOR|a Javé}}: "Fui eu que pequei. Fui eu que fiz o mal. Este povo é como um rebanho de ovelhas. O que eles fizeram para merecer isto? Por favor, castiga a mim e à minha família em lugar deles."

decisions.choice: I ... I: David puts the blame on himself
decisions.reason: The Hebrew adds the pronoun "I" before each verb, which it does not need. The stress falls on David: he, not the people, is the guilty one.

decisions.choice: these sheep: the people in David's care
decisions.reason: David was called from the sheepfolds to shepherd Yahweh's people (5:2; 7:8). He now sees them as a flock suffering for their shepherd's fault.

decisions.choice: what have they done?: David pleads for the people
decisions.reason: David speaks as their king who carries the blame. The narrator has already said that Yahweh's anger was against Israel (verse 1); the text holds both together and does not explain further.

decisions.choice: let your hand be against me and my father's house: punish me and my family
decisions.reason: "Hand" stands for power used in judgment; "my father's house" is David's own family line.

decisions.choice: These people are like sheep; to deserve this; punish me and my family instead
decisions.reason: Readable explains the picture of the sheep, states the sense of David's question, and puts "let your hand be against" in plain words.

source.text: וַיָּבֹא־גָ֥ד אֶל־דָּוִ֖ד בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֑וּא וַיֹּ֣אמֶר ל֗וֹ עֲלֵה֙ הָקֵ֤ם לַֽיהוָה֙ מִזְבֵּ֔חַ בְּגֹ֖רֶן אֲרַ֥וְנָה הַיְבֻסִֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: And came Gad to David on that day and said to him, Go up, set up to Yahweh an altar on [the] threshing floor of Araunah the Jebusite.

en.L: And Gad came to David on that day and said to him, "Go up, raise an altar to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} on the threshing floor of Araunah the Jebusite."
en.B: That same day Gad came to David and told him, "Go up and set up an altar for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} on the threshing floor of Araunah the Jebusite."
en.R: That same day Gad came to David and told him, "Go up to the threshing floor of Araunah the Jebusite. Build an altar to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} there."

es.L: Y Gad vino a David aquel día y le dijo: «Sube, levanta un altar {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}} en la era de Arauna el jebuseo».
es.B: Aquel mismo día Gad vino a David y le dijo: «Sube y levanta un altar {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}} en la era de Arauna el jebuseo».
es.R: Aquel mismo día Gad vino a David y le dijo: «Sube a la era de Arauna el jebuseo. Construye allí un altar {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}}».

fr.L: Et Gad vint vers David ce jour-là et lui dit : « Monte, élève un autel {{divine_name:au SEIGNEUR|à Yahvé}} sur l’aire d’Aravna le Jébusien. »
fr.B: Ce jour-là, Gad vint trouver David et lui dit : « Monte et dresse un autel {{divine_name:au SEIGNEUR|à Yahvé}} sur l’aire d’Aravna le Jébusien. »
fr.R: Le même jour, Gad est venu voir David et lui a dit : « Monte jusqu’à l’aire d’Aravna le Jébusien. Construis là un autel {{divine_name:au SEIGNEUR|à Yahvé}}. »

sw.L: Gadi akaja kwa Daudi siku ile akamwambia, "Panda, umjengee {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} madhabahu katika uwanja wa kupuria wa Arauna Myebusi."
sw.B: Siku ile ile Gadi akaja kwa Daudi akamwambia, "Panda ukamjengee {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} madhabahu katika uwanja wa kupuria wa Arauna Myebusi."
sw.R: Siku ile ile Gadi akaja kwa Daudi akamwambia, "Panda uende kwenye uwanja wa kupuria wa Arauna Myebusi. Mjengee {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} madhabahu huko."

vi.L: Ngày ấy Gát đến gặp Đa-vít và nói với vua: "Xin vua hãy đi lên, lập một bàn thờ cho {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} trên sân đập lúa của A-rau-na người Giê-bu-sít."
vi.B: Ngay ngày hôm ấy Gát đến gặp Đa-vít và thưa: "Xin bệ hạ đi lên lập một bàn thờ cho {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} trên sân đập lúa của A-rau-na người Giê-bu-sít."
vi.R: Ngay ngày hôm ấy Gát đến gặp Đa-vít và thưa: "Xin đức vua đi lên sân đập lúa của A-rau-na người Giê-bu-sít. Hãy xây một bàn thờ cho {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} tại đó."

ko.L: 그날 갓이 다윗에게 와서 말했다. "올라가셔서 여부스 사람 아라우나의 타작마당에 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께 제단을 쌓으십시오."
ko.B: 그날 갓이 다윗에게 와서 말했다. "올라가셔서 여부스 사람 아라우나의 타작마당에 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}를 위한 제단을 세우십시오."
ko.R: 그날 갓이 다윗에게 와서 말했다. "여부스 사람 아라우나의 타작마당으로 올라가십시오. 거기에 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께 드리는 제단을 쌓으십시오."

pt.L: E Gade veio a Davi naquele dia e lhe disse: "Suba, levante um altar {{divine_name:ao SENHOR|a Javé}} na eira de Araúna, o jebuseu."
pt.B: Naquele mesmo dia Gade foi até Davi e lhe disse: "Suba e erga um altar {{divine_name:ao SENHOR|a Javé}} na eira de Araúna, o jebuseu."
pt.R: Naquele mesmo dia Gade foi até Davi e lhe disse: "Suba até a eira de Araúna, o jebuseu. Construa ali um altar {{divine_name:ao SENHOR|a Javé}}."

decisions.choice: go up: the threshing floor lay higher than David's city
decisions.reason: The city of David stood on the lower ridge; the threshing floor was on the hill to its north, where Solomon later built the temple (2 Chronicles 3:1).

decisions.choice: Araunah: the name as the reading tradition gives it
decisions.reason: The written Hebrew spells the name differently here; see the note at verse 16.

decisions.choice: raise an altar: the place where the angel stopped becomes a place of sacrifice
decisions.reason: The altar is to stand where the angel of Yahweh stood (verse 16). Yahweh himself names the place of worship, as the law required (Deuteronomy 12:5).

decisions.choice: Go up to the threshing floor ... Build an altar ... there
decisions.reason: Readable names the place first and splits the command into two sentences.

source.text: וַיַּ֤עַל דָּוִד֙ כִּדְבַר־גָּ֔ד כַּאֲשֶׁ֖ר צִוָּ֥ה יְהוָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And went up David according to [the] word of Gad, as commanded Yahweh.

en.L: And David went up according to the word of Gad, as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had commanded.
en.B: So David went up as Gad had told him, just as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had commanded.
en.R: So David went up, doing what Gad had told him. This was what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had commanded.

es.L: Y David subió conforme a la palabra de Gad, como {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} había mandado.
es.B: Así que David subió como Gad le había dicho, tal como {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} había mandado.
es.R: Así que David subió e hizo lo que Gad le había dicho. Eso era lo que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} había mandado.

fr.L: Et David monta selon la parole de Gad, comme {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} l’avait ordonné.
fr.B: David monta donc comme Gad le lui avait dit, ainsi que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} l’avait ordonné.
fr.R: David est donc monté, en faisant ce que Gad lui avait dit. C’était ce que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} avait ordonné.

sw.L: Daudi akapanda kwa kadiri ya neno la Gadi, kama {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alivyoamuru.
sw.B: Basi Daudi akapanda kama Gadi alivyomwambia, sawasawa na {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alivyoamuru.
sw.R: Basi Daudi akapanda, akafanya kama Gadi alivyomwambia. Hivyo ndivyo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alivyoamuru.

vi.L: Đa-vít đi lên theo lời Gát, như {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đã truyền.
vi.B: Vậy Đa-vít đi lên như Gát đã bảo, đúng như {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đã truyền.
vi.R: Vậy Đa-vít đi lên, làm theo lời Gát đã bảo. Đó là điều {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đã truyền.

ko.L: 다윗은 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 명령하신 대로 갓의 말을 따라 올라갔다.
ko.B: 그래서 다윗은 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 명령하신 그대로, 갓이 말한 대로 올라갔다.
ko.R: 그래서 다윗은 갓이 말한 대로 올라갔다. 그것은 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 명령하신 일이었다.

pt.L: E Davi subiu conforme a palavra de Gade, como {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} tinha ordenado.
pt.B: Então Davi subiu como Gade lhe tinha dito, exatamente como {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} tinha ordenado.
pt.R: Então Davi subiu, fazendo o que Gade lhe tinha dito. Era isso que {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} tinha ordenado.

decisions.choice: according to the word of Gad, as Yahweh commanded: the prophet's word is Yahweh's command
decisions.reason: David obeys at once. The narrator makes clear that Gad spoke for Yahweh.

source.text: וַיַּשְׁקֵ֣ף אֲרַ֗וְנָה וַיַּ֤רְא אֶת־הַמֶּ֨לֶךְ֙ וְאֶת־עֲבָדָ֔יו עֹבְרִ֖ים עָלָ֑יו וַיֵּצֵ֣א אֲרַ֔וְנָה וַיִּשְׁתַּ֧חוּ לַמֶּ֛לֶךְ אַפָּ֖יו אָֽרְצָה׃

records.literal_gloss: And looked down Araunah and saw the king and his servants passing over toward him, and went out Araunah and bowed down to the king [with] his face to [the] ground.

en.L: And Araunah looked down and saw the king and his servants coming over toward him; and Araunah went out and bowed down to the king [with] his face to the ground.
en.B: When Araunah looked down and saw the king and his officials coming toward him, he went out and bowed before the king with his face to the ground.
en.R: Araunah looked down and saw the king and his officials coming toward him. So he went out and bowed down in front of the king with his face to the ground.

es.L: Y Arauna miró y vio al rey y a sus siervos que venían hacia él; y Arauna salió y se postró ante el rey [con] su rostro en tierra.
es.B: Cuando Arauna miró hacia abajo y vio al rey y a sus oficiales que venían hacia él, salió y se postró ante el rey con el rostro en tierra.
es.R: Arauna miró hacia abajo y vio al rey y a sus oficiales que venían hacia él. Entonces salió y se inclinó delante del rey con el rostro en tierra.

fr.L: Et Aravna regarda et vit le roi et ses serviteurs qui passaient vers lui ; et Aravna sortit et se prosterna devant le roi, le visage contre terre.
fr.B: Quand Aravna regarda d’en haut et vit le roi et ses officiers qui venaient vers lui, il sortit et se prosterna devant le roi, le visage contre terre.
fr.R: Aravna a regardé d’en haut et il a vu le roi et ses officiers qui venaient vers lui. Alors il est sorti et s’est incliné devant le roi, le visage contre le sol.

sw.L: Arauna akatazama chini akamwona mfalme na watumishi wake wakivuka kuja kwake; Arauna akatoka akamsujudia mfalme kifudifudi hadi chini.
sw.B: Arauna alipotazama chini na kumwona mfalme na maafisa wake wakija kwake, akatoka akainama mbele ya mfalme kifudifudi hadi chini.
sw.R: Arauna akatazama chini, akamwona mfalme na maafisa wake wakija kwake. Basi akatoka, akainama mbele ya mfalme mpaka uso wake ukagusa ardhi.

vi.L: A-rau-na nhìn xuống và thấy vua cùng các đầy tớ vua đang đi qua về phía mình; A-rau-na đi ra và sấp mặt xuống đất lạy vua.
vi.B: Khi A-rau-na nhìn xuống và thấy vua cùng quần thần đang đi về phía mình, ông liền đi ra sấp mặt xuống đất lạy vua.
vi.R: A-rau-na nhìn xuống và thấy vua cùng quần thần đang đi về phía mình. Vậy ông đi ra và cúi sấp mặt xuống đất trước mặt vua.

ko.L: 아라우나가 내려다보니 왕과 그의 신하들이 자기 쪽으로 건너오고 있었다. 아라우나가 나가서 얼굴을 땅에 대고 왕에게 절했다.
ko.B: 아라우나가 내려다보다가 왕과 그의 신하들이 자기에게로 오는 것을 보고, 나가서 얼굴을 땅에 대고 왕 앞에 엎드려 절했다.
ko.R: 아라우나가 내려다보니 왕과 그의 신하들이 자기 쪽으로 오고 있었다. 그래서 그는 나가서 얼굴을 땅에 대고 왕 앞에 엎드려 절했다.

pt.L: E Araúna olhou do alto e viu o rei e os seus servos que vinham em direção a ele; e Araúna saiu e se prostrou diante do rei com o rosto em terra.
pt.B: Quando Araúna olhou lá de cima e viu o rei e os seus oficiais vindo na sua direção, saiu e se prostrou diante do rei com o rosto em terra.
pt.R: Araúna olhou lá de cima e viu o rei e os seus oficiais vindo na direção dele. Então ele saiu e se curvou diante do rei com o rosto no chão.

decisions.choice: looked down: looked out from a higher place
decisions.reason: The verb is used of looking down from a height or through a window. From the threshing floor above the city, Araunah sees the king's party climbing toward him. 1 Chronicles 21:20 adds that he was threshing wheat and that his four sons hid when they saw the angel.

decisions.choice: bowed down with his face to the ground: the full honor given to a king
decisions.reason: This deep bow, lying face down, was how a subject greeted a king (14:4; 1 Samuel 25:23).

decisions.choice: his officials
decisions.reason: These are the king's court officials, not household servants; the word is rendered as elsewhere in Samuel.

source.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֲרַ֔וְנָה מַדּ֛וּעַ בָּ֥א אֲדֹנִֽי־הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ אֶל־עַבְדּ֑וֹ וַיֹּ֨אמֶר דָּוִ֜ד לִקְנ֧וֹת מֵעִמְּךָ֣ אֶת־הַגֹּ֗רֶן לִבְנ֤וֹת מִזְבֵּ֨חַ֙ לַֽיהוָ֔ה וְתֵעָצַ֥ר הַמַּגֵּפָ֖ה מֵעַ֥ל הָעָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And said Araunah, Why has come my lord the king to his servant? And said David, To buy from you the threshing floor, to build an altar to Yahweh, and may be held back the plague from on the people.

en.L: And Araunah said, "Why has my lord the king come to his servant?" And David said, "To buy the threshing floor from you, to build an altar to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, so that the plague may be held back from the people."
en.B: Araunah asked, "Why has my lord the king come to his servant?" David answered, "To buy your threshing floor, so that I can build an altar to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and the plague on the people may be stopped."
en.R: Araunah asked, "My lord the king, why have you come to me?" David answered, "I have come to buy your threshing floor. I want to build an altar to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} there, so that the plague on the people will stop."

es.L: Y Arauna dijo: «¿Por qué viene mi señor el rey a su siervo?». Y David dijo: «Para comprarte la era, para edificar un altar {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}}, a fin de que la plaga se detenga de sobre el pueblo».
es.B: Arauna le preguntó: «¿Por qué viene mi señor el rey a su siervo?». David le respondió: «Para comprarte la era, a fin de construir un altar {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}} y que se detenga la plaga que ha caído sobre el pueblo».
es.R: Arauna le preguntó: «Mi señor el rey, ¿por qué has venido a verme?». David le respondió: «He venido a comprarte la era. Quiero construir allí un altar {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}}, para que se detenga la plaga que ha caído sobre la gente».

fr.L: Et Aravna dit : « Pourquoi mon seigneur le roi est-il venu vers son serviteur ? » Et David dit : « Pour acheter de toi l’aire, afin d’y bâtir un autel {{divine_name:au SEIGNEUR|à Yahvé}}, et que le fléau soit arrêté de dessus le peuple. »
fr.B: Aravna demanda : « Pourquoi mon seigneur le roi vient-il chez son serviteur ? » David répondit : « Pour t’acheter ton aire, afin d’y bâtir un autel {{divine_name:au SEIGNEUR|à Yahvé}} et que le fléau qui frappe le peuple soit arrêté. »
fr.R: Aravna a demandé : « Mon seigneur le roi, pourquoi es-tu venu chez moi ? » David a répondu : « Je suis venu acheter ton aire. Je veux y construire un autel {{divine_name:au SEIGNEUR|à Yahvé}}, pour que le fléau qui frappe le peuple s’arrête. »

sw.L: Arauna akasema, "Kwa nini bwana wangu mfalme amekuja kwa mtumishi wake?" Daudi akasema, "Ili kununua uwanja wa kupuria kwako, nimjengee {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} madhabahu, ili tauni izuiliwe isiwapate watu."
sw.B: Arauna akauliza, "Kwa nini bwana wangu mfalme amekuja kwa mtumishi wake?" Daudi akajibu, "Nimekuja kununua uwanja wako wa kupuria, ili nimjengee {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} madhabahu na tauni iliyowapata watu ikomeshwe."
sw.R: Arauna akauliza, "Bwana wangu mfalme, kwa nini umekuja kwangu?" Daudi akajibu, "Nimekuja kununua uwanja wako wa kupuria. Nataka kumjengea {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} madhabahu hapo, ili tauni iliyowapata watu ikome."

vi.L: A-rau-na nói: "Sao chúa tôi là vua lại đến với đầy tớ của mình?" Đa-vít nói: "[Ta đến] để mua sân đập lúa của ông, để xây một bàn thờ cho {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, hầu cho tai họa trên dân chúng được ngăn lại."
vi.B: A-rau-na thưa: "Sao bệ hạ lại đến với đầy tớ của mình?" Đa-vít đáp: "Ta đến để mua sân đập lúa của ông, để xây một bàn thờ cho {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, hầu cho tai họa trên dân chúng được chấm dứt."
vi.R: A-rau-na thưa: "Thưa đức vua, sao đức vua lại đến với tôi?" Đa-vít trả lời: "Ta đến để mua sân đập lúa của ông. Ta muốn xây một bàn thờ cho {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} tại đó, để tai họa trên dân chúng chấm dứt."

ko.L: 아라우나가 말했다. "내 주 임금님께서 어찌하여 임금님의 종에게 오셨습니까?" 다윗이 말했다. "네게서 타작마당을 사서 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께 제단을 쌓으려고 왔다. 그러면 백성에게 내린 재앙이 그칠 것이다."
ko.B: 아라우나가 물었다. "내 주 임금님께서 어찌하여 이 종에게 오셨습니까?" 다윗이 대답했다. "네 타작마당을 사려고 왔다. 거기에 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께 제단을 쌓아 백성에게 내린 재앙이 그치게 하려는 것이다."
ko.R: 아라우나가 물었다. "내 주 임금님, 어찌하여 저에게 오셨습니까?" 다윗이 대답했다. "네 타작마당을 사려고 왔다. 거기에 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께 제단을 쌓으려고 한다. 그러면 백성에게 내린 재앙이 그칠 것이다."

pt.L: E Araúna disse: "Por que o meu senhor, o rei, veio ao seu servo?" E Davi disse: "Para comprar de você a eira, para construir um altar {{divine_name:ao SENHOR|a Javé}}, para que a praga seja detida de sobre o povo."
pt.B: Araúna perguntou: "Por que o meu senhor, o rei, veio ao seu servo?" Davi respondeu: "Para comprar a sua eira, para que eu construa um altar {{divine_name:ao SENHOR|a Javé}} e a praga que está sobre o povo seja detida."
pt.R: Araúna perguntou: "Meu senhor, o rei, por que o senhor veio até mim?" Davi respondeu: "Vim comprar a sua eira. Quero construir ali um altar {{divine_name:ao SENHOR|a Javé}}, para que a praga sobre o povo acabe."

decisions.choice: my lord the king ... his servant: the polite speech of a subject
decisions.reason: Araunah speaks of the king and of himself in the third person, the courteous form used in a king's presence (verse 3).

decisions.choice: held back: stopped
decisions.reason: The same verb is used when the plague was stopped after Aaron made atonement (Numbers 17:13, 15). The altar and its offering are to end the plague.

decisions.choice: the plague: a blow struck by Yahweh
decisions.reason: This word, different from "pestilence" in verses 13 and 15, means a blow or striking, and is used of plagues sent as judgment (Numbers 17:13-15; 25:8-9).

decisions.choice: me
decisions.reason: Readable lets Araunah say "me" for the polite "his servant", and speak to the king directly.

decisions.choice: Araunah says "đầy tớ của mình" (L, B) and "tôi" (R); David says "ta" and "ông"
decisions.reason: Araunah uses the court forms of the Samuel terms note; the king speaks politely to the owner of the land he wants to buy.

decisions.choice: a praga seja detida (L, B)
decisions.reason: The verb is the one used when the plague was stopped after Aaron's atonement (m2), and Numbers 17:13 in Portuguese says "a praga foi detida", so Literal and Balanced keep "detida" here and in verse 25. Araunah speaks in the courtly third person, "o meu senhor, o rei" and "o seu servo" (m1); David answers with "você".

source.text: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר אֲרַ֨וְנָה֙ אֶל־דָּוִ֔ד יִקַּ֥ח וְיַ֛עַל אֲדֹנִ֥י הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ הַטּ֣וֹב בְּעֵינָ֑יו רְאֵה֙ הַבָּקָ֣ר לָעֹלָ֔ה וְהַמֹּרִגִּ֛ים וּכְלֵ֥י הַבָּקָ֖ר לָעֵצִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: And said Araunah to David, Let take and offer up my lord the king the good in his eyes; see the oxen for the burnt offering, and the threshing sledges and [the] equipment of the oxen for the wood.

en.L: And Araunah said to David, "Let my lord the king take and offer up what [is] good in his eyes. See, the oxen for the burnt offering, and the threshing sledges and the equipment of the oxen for the wood.
en.B: Araunah said to David, "Let my lord the king take whatever he thinks best and offer it up. Look, here are the oxen for the burnt offering, and the threshing sledges and the oxen's yokes for the wood.
en.R: Araunah said to David, "My king, take whatever you want and offer it as a sacrifice. Here are oxen for the burnt offering. You can use the wooden threshing sledges and the oxen's yokes as firewood.

es.L: Y Arauna dijo a David: «Tome mi señor el rey y ofrezca lo que [sea] bueno a sus ojos. Mira, los bueyes para el holocausto, y los trillos y los aperos de los bueyes para la leña.
es.B: Arauna le dijo a David: «Que mi señor el rey tome lo que mejor le parezca y lo ofrezca. Mira, aquí están los bueyes para el holocausto, y los trillos y los yugos de los bueyes para la leña.
es.R: Arauna le dijo a David: «Mi rey, toma lo que quieras y ofrécelo en sacrificio. Aquí están los bueyes para el holocausto. Puedes usar los trillos de madera y los yugos de los bueyes como leña.

fr.L: Et Aravna dit à David : « Que mon seigneur le roi prenne et offre ce qui [est] bon à ses yeux. Vois, les bœufs pour l’holocauste, et les traîneaux à battre et l’attelage des bœufs pour le bois.
fr.B: Aravna dit à David : « Que mon seigneur le roi prenne ce qui lui semble bon et l’offre en sacrifice. Voici les bœufs pour l’holocauste, et les traîneaux à battre et les jougs des bœufs pour le bois.
fr.R: Aravna a dit à David : « Mon roi, prends tout ce que tu veux et offre-le en sacrifice. Voici des bœufs pour l’holocauste. Tu peux utiliser les traîneaux en bois qui servent à battre le grain et les jougs des bœufs comme bois pour le feu.

sw.L: Arauna akamwambia Daudi, "Bwana wangu mfalme na achukue na kutoa sadaka yaliyo mema machoni pake. Tazama, ng'ombe kwa ajili ya sadaka ya kuteketezwa, na vifaa vya kupuria na vifaa vya ng'ombe kwa ajili ya kuni.
sw.B: Arauna akamwambia Daudi, "Bwana wangu mfalme na achukue chochote anachoona ni bora, akitoe sadaka. Tazama, hawa hapa ng'ombe kwa ajili ya sadaka ya kuteketezwa, na mbao za kupuria na nira za ng'ombe kwa ajili ya kuni.
sw.R: Arauna akamwambia Daudi, "Mfalme wangu, chukua chochote unachotaka ukitoe kuwa sadaka. Hawa hapa ng'ombe kwa ajili ya sadaka ya kuteketezwa. Unaweza kutumia mbao za kupuria na nira za ng'ombe kuwa kuni.

vi.L: A-rau-na nói với Đa-vít: "Xin chúa tôi là vua lấy và dâng lên điều gì vua thấy là tốt. Kìa, có bò để làm của lễ thiêu, và có bàn đạp lúa cùng ách bò để làm củi.
vi.B: A-rau-na thưa với Đa-vít: "Xin bệ hạ lấy bất cứ thứ gì bệ hạ thấy tốt mà dâng lên. Đây có bò để làm của lễ thiêu, và bàn đạp lúa cùng ách bò để làm củi.
vi.R: A-rau-na thưa với Đa-vít: "Thưa đức vua, xin đức vua lấy bất cứ thứ gì đức vua muốn để dâng làm sinh tế. Đây có bò để làm của lễ thiêu. Đức vua có thể dùng bàn đạp lúa bằng gỗ và ách bò làm củi.

ko.L: 아라우나가 다윗에게 말했다. "내 주 임금님께서 보시기에 좋은 것을 가져다가 바치십시오. 보십시오, 번제로 드릴 소들이 있고, 땔감으로 쓸 타작 썰매와 소의 멍에가 있습니다.
ko.B: 아라우나가 다윗에게 말했다. "내 주 임금님께서 좋게 여기시는 것은 무엇이든 가져다가 바치십시오. 보십시오, 번제물로 드릴 소들이 여기 있고, 땔감으로 쓸 타작 썰매와 소의 멍에도 있습니다.
ko.R: 아라우나가 다윗에게 말했다. "임금님, 원하시는 것은 무엇이든 가져다가 제물로 바치십시오. 여기 번제로 드릴 소들이 있습니다. 나무로 된 타작 썰매와 소의 멍에는 장작으로 쓰시면 됩니다.

pt.L: E Araúna disse a Davi: "Que o meu senhor, o rei, tome e ofereça o que [for] bom aos seus olhos. Veja, os bois para o holocausto, e as tábuas de debulhar e os equipamentos dos bois para a lenha.
pt.B: Araúna disse a Davi: "Que o meu senhor, o rei, tome o que achar melhor e o ofereça. Aqui estão os bois para o holocausto, e as tábuas de debulhar e as cangas dos bois para a lenha.
pt.R: Araúna disse a Davi: "Meu rei, pegue o que quiser e ofereça como sacrifício. Aqui estão bois para o holocausto. O senhor pode usar as tábuas de madeira de debulhar e as cangas dos bois como lenha.

decisions.choice: threshing sledges: heavy wooden boards for threshing
decisions.reason: A threshing sledge was a heavy board with sharp stones or iron set into its underside, dragged by oxen over the grain to break the ears (Isaiah 41:15). Its wood could be burned.

decisions.choice: the equipment of the oxen: their yokes and harness
decisions.reason: The phrase covers the wooden gear the oxen wore to pull the sledges.

decisions.choice: in his eyes: the reading tradition
decisions.reason: The written Hebrew has "in his eye", and the traditional reading "in his eyes". The sense is the same: whatever the king thinks good.

decisions.choice: let my lord the king take and offer up: a polite offer
decisions.reason: Araunah offers the king everything he needs for the sacrifice, without charge, and goes on speaking into the next verse.

decisions.choice: offer it as a sacrifice; You can use ... as firewood
decisions.reason: Readable says plainly what the offering and the wood are for.

decisions.choice: no closing quote mark
decisions.reason: Araunah's speech continues into verse 23, where the quotation closes.

decisions.choice: as tábuas de debulhar
decisions.reason: The sledge was a heavy wooden board dragged over the grain (m1); "trilho", the old Portuguese name, is now understood as a rail, so every level says what it was, "tábuas de debulhar".

records.literal_gloss: All gives Araunah, O king, to the king. And said Araunah to the king, Yahweh your God, may he accept you.

en.L: All [this], O king, Araunah gives to the king." And Araunah said to the king, "May {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God accept you."
en.B: All this, my king, Araunah gives to the king." And Araunah said to the king, "May {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God accept you."
en.R: I, Araunah, give all of this to you, my king." Araunah also said to the king, "I pray that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God will accept your offering."

es.L: Todo [esto], oh rey, Arauna se lo da al rey». Y Arauna dijo al rey: «Que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} tu Dios te acepte».
es.B: Todo esto, mi rey, Arauna se lo da al rey». Y Arauna le dijo al rey: «Que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} tu Dios te acepte».

fr.L: Tout [cela], ô roi, Aravna le donne au roi. » Et Aravna dit au roi : « Que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} ton Dieu t’accueille favorablement ! »
fr.B: Tout cela, ô roi, Aravna le donne au roi. » Et Aravna dit au roi : « Que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} ton Dieu t’accueille avec faveur ! »
fr.R: Moi, Aravna, je te donne tout cela, mon roi. » Aravna a aussi dit au roi : « Je prie pour que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} ton Dieu accepte ton offrande. »

decisions.choice: All this, O king, Araunah gives to the king: Araunah is still speaking
alternatives: Araunah gave everything to the king
Araunah the king gave everything to the king
decisions.reason: The words can be read as the end of Araunah's speech, in which he calls himself by name as he called himself "his servant" (verse 21), with "O king" as an address. They can also be read as the narrator's words, "Araunah gave everything to the king", or as "Araunah the king gave everything to the king", which would make Araunah a Jebusite ruler. The verb form can mean either "gives" or "gave".

decisions.choice: accept you: receive you and your offering with favor
decisions.reason: The verb is used of God accepting an offering and the one who brings it (Leviticus 1:4; Ezekiel 20:40-41).

decisions.choice: I, Araunah; accept your offering
decisions.reason: Readable has Araunah speak in the first person and makes clear that the acceptance is of David's offering.

records.literal_gloss: And said the king to Araunah, No, for surely I will buy [it] from you for a price, and I will not offer up to Yahweh my God burnt offerings without cost. And bought David the threshing floor and the oxen for silver, fifty shekels.

en.L: But the king said to Araunah, "No, for I will surely buy [it] from you for a price; I will not offer up to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} my God burnt offerings without cost." So David bought the threshing floor and the oxen for silver, fifty shekels.
en.B: But the king said to Araunah, "No, I insist on paying you a price for it. I will not offer {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} my God burnt offerings at no cost to myself." So David bought the threshing floor and the oxen for {{units:about 1 1/4 pounds of silver|fifty shekels of silver}}.
en.R: But the king answered Araunah, "No, I will pay you for it. I will not give burnt offerings to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} my God that I got for free." So David bought the threshing floor and the oxen. He paid {{units:about 1 1/4 pounds of silver|fifty shekels of silver}} for them.

fr.B: Mais le roi répondit à Aravna : « Non, je tiens à te la payer. Je n’offrirai pas {{divine_name:au SEIGNEUR|à Yahvé}} mon Dieu des holocaustes qui ne m’aient rien coûté. » David acheta donc l’aire et les bœufs pour {{units:environ 575 grammes d’argent|cinquante sicles d’argent}}.

decisions.choice: I will surely buy: David insists
decisions.reason: The Hebrew repeats the verb ("buying I will buy") for emphasis. David will not accept the gift.

decisions.choice: burnt offerings without cost: a sacrifice must cost the one who offers it
decisions.reason: An offering made from someone else's property would not be David's own gift. Abraham likewise insisted on paying full price for the field of Machpelah (Genesis 23:13).

decisions.choice: fifty shekels of silver: the price of the threshing floor and the oxen
decisions.reason: 1 Chronicles 21:25 says David paid 600 shekels of gold for "the place". The two figures may refer to different purchases, this one to the threshing floor and the oxen, the other to the whole site on which the temple was later built, or the difference may come from the way the story was passed down. The text does not explain it.

decisions.choice: silver, fifty shekels: silver weighed out by the shekel
decisions.reason: Payment was made in silver by weight; a shekel was a weight of about 2/5 ounce, not a coin.

decisions.choice: about 1 1/4 pounds of silver (default); fifty shekels of silver (alternative)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the modern weight with the shekel as the alternative. Literal keeps the Hebrew unit.

decisions.choice: at no cost to myself (Balanced); that I got for free (Readable)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew word means "for nothing, without payment"; the wording makes clear that the cost is David's.

en.L: And David built there an altar to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and offered up burnt offerings and peace offerings. And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} was moved by prayer for the land, and the plague was held back from Israel.
en.B: David built an altar to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} there and sacrificed burnt offerings and peace offerings. Then {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} answered the prayers for the land, and the plague on Israel was stopped.

decisions.choice: Yahweh was entreated for the land: the same words that close the famine story in 21:14
decisions.reason: Both stories of national disaster (21:1-14 and this chapter) end with these words. The verb means that Yahweh let himself be moved by prayer and answered it.

decisions.choice: burnt offerings and peace offerings
decisions.reason: A burnt offering was given wholly to Yahweh on the altar; a peace offering was shared in a meal by the worshipers (Leviticus 1; 3). Together they mark restored peace with God.

decisions.choice: an altar there: the place of the later temple
decisions.reason: The book ends with David building an altar at the place where Solomon would build the temple (1 Chronicles 22:1; 2 Chronicles 3:1).

decisions.choice: answered the prayers for the land
decisions.reason: The Hebrew verb is passive, "was entreated": Yahweh let himself be moved by prayer. Literal says "was moved by prayer"; Balanced and Readable say it in active words.

decisions.choice: "se laissa fléchir en faveur du pays" (L); "exauça les prières pour le pays" (B, R)
alternatives: a different wording in each chapter
decisions.reason: The same words close the famine story in 21:14 (m1), and French uses the same wording in both places so that the echo is kept.

decisions.choice: "của lễ thiêu"; "tế lễ bình an"
decisions.reason: The Genesis terms note's word for the burnt offering, and the usual Vietnamese name for the peace offering.

decisions.choice: se deixou comover pela terra (L); atendeu às orações pela terra (B); respondeu às orações pela terra (R)
decisions.reason: The words that close the famine story in 21:14 (m1) keep the Portuguese wording of that verse, level by level, so the two stories end alike. "Holocaustos" and "sacrifícios de comunhão" are the Pentateuch's terms (m2).
